items.title: Local PVM extension: tensoring a projection-valued measure with the identity
items.statement:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H,K$ be
nonzero complex Hilbert spaces ([[def-hilbert-space]]) and let
$H\widehat\otimes K$ be their completed tensor product with inclusion $\kappa$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]). Let $(X,\Sigma)$ be a
measurable space ([[def-measurable-space]]) and let $E$ be a projection valued
measure on $(X,\Sigma)$ acting on $H$ ([[def-projection-valued-measure]]).
Define, for $B\in\Sigma$,
$$F(B):=E(B)\otimes I_{K}\in\mathcal B(H\widehat\otimes K),$$
the bounded tensor operator of [[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]]
clause (a). Then:

(a) $F$ is a projection valued measure on $(X,\Sigma)$ acting on
$H\widehat\otimes K$;

(b) for every bounded $\Sigma$-measurable function $f:X\to\mathbb C$, writing
$\Phi_{F}(f)=\int f\,dF$ and $\Phi_{E}(f)=\int f\,dE$ for the integrals of
[[thm-bounded-borel-pvm-integral]], one has
$$\Phi_{F}(f)=\Phi_{E}(f)\otimes I_{K};$$

(c) if $(S_{n})$ is a sequence of bounded operators on $H$ with
$\sup_{n}\|S_{n}\|<+\infty$ and $S_{n}x\to Sx$ for every $x\in H$, then
$(S_{n}\otimes I_{K})z\to(S\otimes I_{K})z$ for every
$z\in H\widehat\otimes K$;

(d) if $X$ is a locally compact Hausdorff space ([[def-locally-compact-space]]),
$\Sigma$ its Borel $\sigma$-algebra ([[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]) and $E$
regular in the sense of [[def-projection-valued-measure]], then $F$ is regular.

Clause (d) is what makes $F$ a regular projection valued measure on
$\mathbb R$ in the application to assigned sharp observables, so that the
converse direction of the spectral theorem supplies a self-adjoint operator
having $F$ as its spectral measure. No assertion is made about unbounded
operators in this lemma itself.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The Axiom of Countable Choice; nonzero complex Hilbert spaces $H,K$; the completed tensor product $H\widehat\otimes K$ with inclusion $\kappa$; a measurable space $(X,\Sigma)$; a projection valued measure $E$ on $(X,\Sigma)$; the operators $S_{n},S\in\mathcal B(H)$; a bounded measurable $f:X\to\mathbb C$.

[F1] **Tensor-product maps.** By [[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]] clauses (a)-(d), for all bounded $S\in\mathcal B(H,H')$, $T\in\mathcal B(K,K')$ there is a unique bounded $S\otimes T$ with $(S\otimes T)\kappa(u\otimes v)=\kappa'(Su\otimes Tv)$, satisfying $\|S\otimes T\|\le\|S\|\,\|T\|$ ([[def-operator-norm]]), $(S\otimes T)^{*}=S^{*}\otimes T^{*}$ and $(S\otimes T)(S'\otimes T')=(SS')\otimes(TT')$; the assignment is linear in each argument, and $\kappa[H\odot K]$ is dense in $H\widehat\otimes K$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]] clause (c)).

[F2] **Projection valued measure.** $E(B)$ is an orthogonal projection on $H$ for every $B\in\Sigma$ ([[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]]), $E(\varnothing)=0$, $E(X)=I$, $E(B\cap C)=E(B)E(C)$, and for pairwise disjoint $B_{n}$ with union $B$ one has $E(B)x=\sum_{n}E(B_{n})x$ in norm for every $x\in H$ ([[def-projection-valued-measure]]).

[F3] **Bounded PVM integral.** For bounded measurable $f$ there is a unique bounded $\Phi_{E}(f)=\int f\,dE$ with $\langle\Phi_{E}(f)x,y\rangle=\int f\,dE_{x,y}$; for every sequence of complex simple functions $s_{n}$ with $\|f-s_{n}\|_{\infty}\to0$ one has $\|\Phi_{E}(f)-\int s_{n}\,dE\|\to0$, and $\|\Phi_{E}(f)\|\le\|f\|_{\infty}$ ([[thm-bounded-borel-pvm-integral]]).

[F4] **Regular projection valued measures.** When $X$ is locally compact Hausdorff and $\Sigma$ its Borel $\sigma$-algebra, $E$ is regular exactly when every finite positive measure $E_{x}(B)=\langle E(B)x,x\rangle$ is a regular Borel measure: Radon, meaning finite on compact sets, outer regular on Borel sets and inner regular on open sets ([[def-radon-measure-on-an-lch-space]]), and inner regular on every Borel set ([[def-regular-borel-measure-on-an-lch-space]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; build the tensor family $F=E\otimes I$ from the
bounded tensor calculus, transfer finite additivity and strong countable
additivity to it, extend the integral identity from simple functions to
bounded measurable functions by uniform approximation, and prove regularity
of the scalar measures of $F$ first on finite algebraic tensors and then on
the whole completed product by density.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F4].

1.1 [Strong continuity of tensoring with the identity] Let $M:=\sup_{n}\|S_{n}\|<+\infty$. Strong convergence gives $\|Sx\|=\lim_{n}\|S_{n}x\|\le M\|x\|$ for every $x\in H$, so $\|S\|\le M$. For $z\in H\widehat\otimes K$ and $\varepsilon>0$, density [F1] gives a finite sum $z_{0}=\kappa\bigl(\sum_{i=1}^{m}u_{i}\otimes v_{i}\bigr)$ with $\|z-z_{0}\|<\varepsilon/(4M+1)$. By linearity and the norm estimate [F1], $\|(S_{n}\otimes I)-(S\otimes I)\|\le M+\|S\|\le2M$, and hence $\|((S_{n}\otimes I)-(S\otimes I))(z-z_{0})\|<\varepsilon/2$ for every $n$ (also when $M=0$, when the left side is zero). On the finite sum, [F1] gives $\|((S_{n}\otimes I)-(S\otimes I))z_{0}\|\le\sum_{i=1}^{m}\|(S_{n}-S)u_{i}\|\,\|v_{i}\|\to0$. This is less than $\varepsilon/2$ for all large $n$, and the triangle inequality proves (c). [F1, algebra, choose]

1.2 [Projection structure] For $B,C\in\Sigma$ one has $F(B)^{*}=(E(B)\otimes I)^{*}=E(B)^{*}\otimes I^{*}=E(B)\otimes I=F(B)$ and $F(B)^{2}=(E(B)\otimes I)(E(B)\otimes I)=E(B)^{2}\otimes I^{2}=E(B)\otimes I=F(B)$, so $F(B)$ is an orthogonal projection; moreover $F(B\cap C)=(E(B)E(C))\otimes I=(E(B)\otimes I)(E(C)\otimes I)=F(B)F(C)$, $F(\varnothing)=0\otimes I=0$ and $F(X)=I\otimes I=I$. [F1, F2, algebra]

1.3 [Integral identity] For a complex simple function $s=\sum_{k=1}^{m}\alpha_{k}\mathbf 1_{B_{k}}$ with $B_{k}\in\Sigma$ pairwise disjoint, linearity of $S\mapsto S\otimes I$ and of the integral [F1, F3] give $\Phi_{F}(s)=\sum_{k}\alpha_{k}F(B_{k})=\sum_{k}\alpha_{k}(E(B_{k})\otimes I)=\bigl(\sum_{k}\alpha_{k}E(B_{k})\bigr)\otimes I=\Phi_{E}(s)\otimes I$. For bounded measurable $f$ choose simple $s_{n}$ with $\|f-s_{n}\|_{\infty}\le 2^{-n}$ by the explicit rounding construction on the finite range of $f$; the norm bounds [F1, F3] give $\|\Phi_{F}(f)-\Phi_{F}(s_{n})\|\le\|f-s_{n}\|_{\infty}\to0$ and $\|\Phi_{E}(f)\otimes I-\Phi_{E}(s_{n})\otimes I\|\le\|f-s_{n}\|_{\infty}\to0$, so uniqueness of limits yields $\Phi_{F}(f)=\Phi_{E}(f)\otimes I$, which is (b). [F1, F3, construct, algebra]

1.4 [Regularity on finite algebraic tensors] Assume $X$ locally compact Hausdorff with Borel $\sigma$-algebra and $E$ regular, and let $z_{0}=\kappa\bigl(\sum_{i=1}^{m}u_{i}\otimes v_{i}\bigr)$. Put $C:=\sum_{i=1}^{m}\|v_{i}\|^{2}$. If $m=0$ or $C=0$, then $z_{0}=0$, so $\nu_{z_{0}}$ is the zero measure and is inner regular on every Borel set, taking the compact set $\varnothing$. Otherwise $m\ge1$ and $C>0$. For Borel $B$, $F(B)z_{0}=\kappa\bigl(\sum_{i=1}^{m}E(B)u_{i}\otimes v_{i}\bigr)$ by [F1], so the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality for the Euclidean pairing gives $\nu_{z_{0}}(B):=\langle F(B)z_{0},z_{0}\rangle=\bigl\|\sum_{i}E(B)u_{i}\otimes v_{i}\bigr\|^{2}\le C\sum_{i}\langle E(B)u_{i},u_{i}\rangle$; also $\nu_{z_{0}}(X)=\|z_{0}\|^{2}<+\infty$. Given $\varepsilon>0$, each finite measure $\langle E(\cdot)u_{i},u_{i}\rangle$ is regular by [F4], so there are compact $K_{i}\subseteq B$ with $\langle E(B\setminus K_{i})u_{i},u_{i}\rangle<\varepsilon/(mC)$; for the compact $K=\bigcup_{i}K_{i}$ one has $B\setminus K\subseteq B\setminus K_{i}$ and hence $\nu_{z_{0}}(B)-\nu_{z_{0}}(K)=\nu_{z_{0}}(B\setminus K)\le C\sum_{i}\langle E(B\setminus K_{i})u_{i},u_{i}\rangle<\varepsilon$. Thus $\nu_{z_{0}}$ is inner regular on Borel sets. [F1, F4, algebra, choose]

2.1 [Strong countable additivity] Let $(B_{n})$ be pairwise disjoint with union $B$. For finite $N$ the multiplicativity of step 1.2 and $F(B_{i})F(B_{j})=F(B_{i}\cap B_{j})=0$ for $i\ne j$ give $\sum_{n\le N}F(B_{n})=F(\bigcup_{n\le N}B_{n})=E(\bigcup_{n\le N}B_{n})\otimes I$. The orthogonal projections $E(\bigcup_{n\le N}B_{n})$ are uniformly bounded by one and converge strongly to $E(B)$ by [F2], so step 1.1 gives $\sum_{n\le N}F(B_{n})\to F(B)$ strongly; with step 1.2 this is (a). [F1, F2, step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 [Regularity on the completed product] Keep the hypotheses of step 1.4 and let $z\in H\widehat\otimes K$, $B$ Borel, $\varepsilon>0$; if $z=0$ there is nothing to prove, so let $z\ne0$ and choose $z_{0}=\kappa(\sum_{i}u_{i}\otimes v_{i})$ with $\|z-z_{0}\|\le\sqrt{\varepsilon}/2$ by [F1], then a compact $K\subseteq B$ with $\nu_{z_{0}}(B\setminus K)\le\varepsilon/4$ by step 1.4. Since $F$ is projection valued by step 2.1, $\nu_{z}(B)-\nu_{z}(K)=\|F(B\setminus K)z\|^{2}\le\bigl(\|F(B\setminus K)(z-z_{0})\|+\|F(B\setminus K)z_{0}\|\bigr)^{2}\le\bigl(\sqrt{\varepsilon}/2+\sqrt{\varepsilon}/2\bigr)^{2}=\varepsilon$, so $\nu_{z}$ is inner regular on Borel sets; it is finite since $\nu_{z}(X)=\|z\|^{2}<+\infty$. Inner regularity applied to the complement gives outer regularity: for Borel $E_{0}$ and $\eta>0$ choose compact $L\subseteq X\setminus E_{0}$ with $\nu_{z}(X\setminus E_{0})-\nu_{z}(L)<\eta$, so the open $V=X\setminus L$ contains $E_{0}$ and $\nu_{z}(V)<\nu_{z}(E_{0})+\eta$. Hence every $F_{z}$ is a regular Borel measure and $F$ is regular, which is (d). [F1, F4, step 2.1, step 1.4, algebra, choose]

4.1 [Assembly] Step 2.1 proves (a), step 1.3 proves (b), step 1.1 proves (c) and steps 1.4 and 3.1 prove (d). [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 1.3, step 3.1] ∎

## Remarks

- **Use.** The lemma is the mathematical core of the local readout of a
  subsystem quantity: on a composite $H\widehat\otimes K$, the outcome
  structure of a quantity of the first factor alone is $E(\cdot)\otimes I_{K}$,
  and by clause (d) together with the converse direction of the spectral
  theorem it is the spectral measure of a self-adjoint operator on the
  composite. Nothing here is a physical statement about measurements; the
  physical reading is fixed on the composites page.
- **Countable Choice.** The choice hypothesis enters through the tensor
  construction and is carried as stated; clause (c) additionally uses the
  density of the algebraic tensor product, which is part of that construction.

items.title: Pure-state separability is equivalent to being a product: a Schmidt overlap witness
items.statement:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H,K$ be arbitrary nonzero complex Hilbert spaces, with inner products linear in the first argument, and put $L=H\widehat\otimes K$ with the isometric inclusion $\kappa$ of [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]. Write $T_{x,y}z=\langle z,y\rangle x$ as in [[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]]. Set
$$\mathcal P=\{T_{\kappa(a\otimes b),\kappa(a\otimes b)}:\|a\|=\|b\|=1\},\qquad \mathcal S=\overline{\operatorname{conv}\mathcal P}^{\|\cdot\|_1},$$
with trace class as in [[def-trace-class-operator]], where the convex hull consists of finite convex combinations, and the closure is taken in the trace-class operators on $L$. For each unit $\Psi\in L$, let $P_\Psi=T_{\Psi,\Psi}$. Then
$$P_\Psi\in\mathcal S\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \Psi=\kappa(a\otimes b)\text{ for some unit }a\in H,\ b\in K.$$

More precisely, let $\Psi=\sum_{r\in J}s_r\kappa(v_r\otimes u_r)$ be any finite or countably infinite positive Schmidt expansion from [[thm-nrqm-composites-infinite-schmidt-decomposition]], and put $\lambda_r=s_r^2$. The number $m=\max_{r\in J}\lambda_r$ exists. Every pair of unit vectors $a,b$ satisfies $|\langle\Psi,\kappa(a\otimes b)\rangle|^2\le m$, with equality at a Schmidt pair whose weight is $m$. Every $\sigma\in\mathcal S$ satisfies $\operatorname{tr}(\sigma P_\Psi)\le m$, whereas $\operatorname{tr}(P_\Psi^2)=1$. If $\Psi$ is non-product then $m<1$ and, for every $\sigma\in\mathcal S$,
$$\|P_\Psi-\sigma\|_1\ge 1-m>0.$$
The factors need not be separable; only the support of the single tensor vector has a countable Schmidt expansion. These are mathematical trace pairings, with no measurement or Born-rule assumption.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Countable Choice; the Hilbert spaces $H,K$; $L$, $\kappa$, $\mathcal P$, $\mathcal S$ and unit $\Psi$ as above.

[F1] The completed tensor product is Hilbert, $\|\kappa(a\otimes b)\|=\|a\|\|b\|$, and $\langle\kappa(x\otimes y),\kappa(a\otimes b)\rangle=\langle x,a\rangle\langle y,b\rangle$, with linearity in the first argument ([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]] clauses (a), (c)).

[F2] Under Countable Choice, an arbitrary unit tensor vector has a nonempty at most countable positive Schmidt expansion, with orthonormal families $(v_r)$, $(u_r)$ and $\sum_rs_r^2=1$; it is a product vector exactly when there is one positive coefficient ([[thm-nrqm-composites-infinite-schmidt-decomposition]], Statement). No ambient Hilbert basis is assumed.

[F3] Rank-one operators are positive when their two vectors agree, have trace $\operatorname{tr}T_{x,y}=\langle x,y\rangle$, and for trace-class $T$ satisfy $\operatorname{tr}(TT_{x,y})=\langle Tx,y\rangle$. Trace is linear by [[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]] clause 4, and $\|T\|\le\|T\|_1$ by [[thm-trace-class-is-a-two-sided-banach-operator-ideal]] clause 1; the rank-one identities are [[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]] clauses (b), (c), (e).

## Proof

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]–[F3].

1.1 [Maximum and the strict gap] By [F2], $\lambda_r>0$ and $\sum_r\lambda_r=1$. Fix one $r_0\in J$ and put $c=\lambda_{r_0}>0$. The set $E=\{r:\lambda_r\ge c\}$ is nonempty and finite: any finite subset of $E$ with $N$ elements has weight sum at least $Nc\le1$, so $E$ has at most $\lfloor1/c\rfloor$ elements. The maximum $m$ on this finite set is a maximum on $J$, since every weight outside $E$ is below $c\le m$. If $\Psi$ is non-product, [F2] gives at least two positive weights; at an index $r_*$ attaining $m$, another positive weight implies $m<\sum_r\lambda_r=1$. [given, F2, algebra]

1.2 [Finite orthogonal estimates] For an orthonormal family $(e_r)$, a vector $x$ and a finite set $F$, expanding $\|x-\sum_{r\in F}\langle x,e_r\rangle e_r\|^2$ gives $\|x\|^2-\sum_{r\in F}|\langle x,e_r\rangle|^2\ge0$. Thus for unit $a,b$ the sums of $|\langle v_r,a\rangle|^2$ and $|\langle u_r,b\rangle|^2$ are each at most one, using conjugate symmetry and the supremum of finite sums. For finite complex sequences $(\alpha_r),(\beta_r)$, Cauchy–Schwarz gives $|\sum_r\alpha_r\beta_r|\le(\sum_r|\alpha_r|^2)^{1/2}(\sum_r|\beta_r|^2)^{1/2}$: this follows by expanding $\sum_r|\alpha_r-t\overline{\beta_r}|^2\ge0$ with $t=(\sum_r\alpha_r\beta_r)/(\sum_r|\beta_r|^2)$ when the denominator is positive, and is immediate otherwise. [given, F1, algebra]

1.3 [Exact continuity of the fixed trace witness] For every trace-class $T$ on $L$, [F3] gives $\operatorname{tr}(TP_\Psi)=\langle T\Psi,\Psi\rangle$ and $|\operatorname{tr}(TP_\Psi)|\le\|T\Psi\|\|\Psi\|\le\|T\|\le\|T\|_1$, since $\|\Psi\|=1$. Applying this estimate to $T-S$ proves $|\operatorname{tr}(TP_\Psi)-\operatorname{tr}(SP_\Psi)|\le\|T-S\|_1$. Thus this particular bounded trace functional is 1-Lipschitz; no unspecified continuity theorem or unbounded cyclicity is used. Also $P_\Psi\Psi=\Psi$, so $\operatorname{tr}(P_\Psi^2)=\langle P_\Psi\Psi,\Psi\rangle=1$. [given, F3, algebra]

2.1 [The overlap bound, with the conjugations fixed] For a finite Schmidt truncation $\Psi_F$, [F1] gives $\langle\Psi_F,\kappa(a\otimes b)\rangle=\sum_{r\in F}s_r\langle v_r,a\rangle\langle u_r,b\rangle$; equivalently it is the conjugate of $\sum_{r\in F}s_r\langle a,v_r\rangle\langle b,u_r\rangle$. Applying step 1.2 to $\alpha_r=s_r\langle v_r,a\rangle$ and $\beta_r=\langle u_r,b\rangle$ gives a modulus bound $(\sum_{r\in F}\lambda_r|\langle v_r,a\rangle|^2)^{1/2}(\sum_{r\in F}|\langle u_r,b\rangle|^2)^{1/2}\le\sqrt m$. The Schmidt truncations converge in norm [F2], so continuity of the Hilbert pairing passes this bound to $\Psi$. At $a=v_{r_*}$ and $b=u_{r_*}$, orthonormality gives overlap $s_{r_*}$ and squared overlap $m$. [step 1.1, step 1.2, F1, F2, algebra]

3.1 [Convex hull and its closure] For unit product $q=\kappa(a\otimes b)$, [F3] and first-linear conjugate symmetry give $\operatorname{tr}(T_{q,q}P_\Psi)=\langle T_{q,q}\Psi,\Psi\rangle=\langle\Psi,q\rangle\langle q,\Psi\rangle=|\langle\Psi,q\rangle|^2\le m$ by step 2.1. Trace linearity gives the same real bound for finite convex combinations. For $\sigma\in\mathcal S$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, the definition of closure supplies a single $\tau\in\operatorname{conv}\mathcal P$ with $\|\sigma-\tau\|_1<\varepsilon$. Step 1.3 gives $|\operatorname{tr}(\sigma P_\Psi)-\operatorname{tr}(\tau P_\Psi)|<\varepsilon$; letting $\varepsilon\downarrow0$ shows that $\operatorname{tr}(\sigma P_\Psi)$ is real and at most $m$. This neighborhood argument does not select a sequence of approximants. [step 2.1, step 1.3, F3, algebra]

4.1 [Equivalence and distance] If $\Psi$ is non-product, steps 1.1, 1.3 and 3.1 give $\operatorname{tr}(P_\Psi^2)=1>m\ge\operatorname{tr}(\sigma P_\Psi)$ for all $\sigma\in\mathcal S$, so $P_\Psi\notin\mathcal S$. Moreover step 1.3 gives $\|P_\Psi-\sigma\|_1\ge|\operatorname{tr}((P_\Psi-\sigma)P_\Psi)|=1-\operatorname{tr}(\sigma P_\Psi)\ge1-m$. Conversely a unit product vector has $P_\Psi\in\mathcal P\subseteq\mathcal S$. If initially $\Psi=\kappa(x\otimes y)$ with arbitrary nonzero factors, [F1] gives $\|x\|\|y\|=1$; therefore $a=x/\|x\|$ and $b=\|x\|y$ are unit and $\Psi=\kappa(a\otimes b)$. This proves the full claimed equivalence for the declared trace-norm closure and the strict witness bound. [step 1.1, step 1.3, step 3.1, F1, algebra] ∎

items.title: Product vectors, separable states and entangled states of a two-factor composite
items.statement:
## Definition

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H,K$ be
nonzero complex Hilbert spaces ([[def-hilbert-space]]) and let
$H\widehat\otimes K$ be their completed tensor product with inclusion $\kappa$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]). Density operators are
the self-adjoint positive trace-class operators of trace one
([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a),
[[def-trace-class-operator]]), and for $u,u'\in H$, $v,v'\in K$ the rank-one
operator $T_{u\otimes v,\,u'\otimes v'}$ is the one of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]].

**(a) Product vectors and pure product states.** A vector $\Psi\in
H\widehat\otimes K$ is a **product vector** when $\Psi=\kappa(u\otimes v)$ for
some $u\in H$, $v\in K$. A **pure product state** of the composite is a
density operator of the form
$$T_{\Psi,\Psi},\qquad \Psi=\kappa(u\otimes v),\quad \|u\|=\|v\|=1 .$$
A vector is **non-product** when it is not a product vector.

**(b) Separable states.** Write $\mathcal P$ for the set of all pure product
states, a subset of the set $D(H\widehat\otimes K)$ of density operators. The
**separable states** are the elements of the trace-norm closed convex hull
$$\mathcal S(H,K):=\overline{\operatorname{conv}}\,\mathcal P \ \subseteq\ D(H\widehat\otimes K),$$
where $\operatorname{conv}$ denotes the set of finite convex combinations and
the closure is taken in the trace norm $\|\cdot\|_{1}$ of
[[thm-trace-class-is-a-two-sided-banach-operator-ideal]]. A state
$\rho\in D(H\widehat\otimes K)$ is **entangled** (with respect to the
declared splitting $H,K$) when $\rho\notin\mathcal S(H,K)$.

**(c) Conventions and elementary consequences of the form of the definition.**
The set $\operatorname{conv}\mathcal P$ consists exactly of the finite sums
$\sum_{j=1}^{n}w_{j}T_{\Psi_{j},\Psi_{j}}$ with $n\ge1$, weights $w_{j}\ge0$,
$\sum_{j}w_{j}=1$ and unit product vectors $\Psi_{j}$: such sums are convex
combinations of density operators and hence density operators
([[lem-nrqm-state-geometry-density-set-convex-and-complete]] clause (a);
the finite-dimensional case of that clause is the
[[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] expansion
applied to orthogonal pure states).
Every element of $\operatorname{conv}\mathcal P$ is a density operator, and
$\mathcal S(H,K)$ is a convex subset of $D(H\widehat\otimes K)$: if $\rho,\sigma$
are limits of convex combinations $\rho_{n}\to\rho$, $\sigma_{n}\to\sigma$ and
$t\in[0,1]$, then $t\rho+(1-t)\sigma$ is the trace-norm limit of the convex
combinations $t\rho_{n}+(1-t)\sigma_{n}$. Separability of a state is a
property of the declared splitting $(H,K)$; no assertion is made here about
its behaviour under a different factorization of a larger space.

**(d) Finite dimension.** When $H$ and $K$ are finite dimensional,
$\mathcal P$ is compact and $\operatorname{conv}\mathcal P$ is already closed
in the trace norm (it is a compact, hence closed, convex set in the
finite-dimensional space of endomorphisms of $H\widehat\otimes K$), so
$\mathcal S(H,K)=\operatorname{conv}\mathcal P$ and no closure convention is
needed. In the general case the closure in clause (b) is declared explicitly
and is part of the definition.

**(e) Pure-state specialization and status.** A pure state $T_{\Psi,\Psi}$ with $\|\Psi\|=1$ is separable in the precise trace-norm closed-convex-hull sense of clause (b) exactly when $\Psi$ is a product vector of clause (a); otherwise it is entangled. This is the proved mathematical specialization of [[lem-nrqm-composites-pure-state-separability-criterion]], whose locally defined $\mathcal P,\mathcal S$ are exactly those above. Clauses (a)-(e) fix mathematical vocabulary and adopt no physical assumption, dynamics, measurement or probability law. Whether a laboratory preparation realizes a separable or entangled state for the declared splitting remains a tested identification with uncertainty, not a consequence about nature of this definition.

## Remarks

- **Why the closure is explicit.** In infinite dimension the convex hull of
  the pure product states need not be trace-norm closed, and different authors
  complete it differently. Clause (b) declares the trace-norm closure, which
  is the convention used by this category; the mathematical results of the
  page are stated for this declared class.
- **Entanglement is relative to a splitting.** The same vector of a
  three-factor space may be a product vector with respect to one grouping of
  the factors and non-product with respect to another, so a separability or
  entanglement statement without the declared pair $(H,K)$ is incomplete;
  the definition above always carries that pair.

items.title: Composite systems of the framework: product bases, local readouts, local effects and local instruments
items.statement:
## Definition

Adopt the state and composition postulate (P1), the observable and probability
postulate (P2) and the ideal conditional-measurement postulate (P3) of the
framework ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-ideal-conditional-measurement]]), and assume the Axiom
of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice, the choice hypotheses of the cited
mathematical suppliers ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]).
The following vocabulary is used by this page for a declared pair of
distinguishable subsystems.

**(a) Declared composite and its state space.** A **declared composite model**
is the assignment of two declared systems $A$ and $B$ of the massive-matter
sector, their assigned nonzero separable complex Hilbert spaces $H$ and $K$
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] clauses (i) and (iv),
[[def-hilbert-space]]), and the **composite assigned space**
$$H\widehat\otimes K,$$
the completed Hilbert tensor product of $H$ and $K$ with inclusion $\kappa$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]], clause (iv) of P1). The
**state space of the declared composite** is $D(H\widehat\otimes K)$, the set of
density operators on $H\widehat\otimes K$
([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]). A **preparation of the
composite** is an element of this set; the model's assignment of a state to a
preparation is the assignment of clause (iii) of P1, not a consequence of this
definition.

**(b) Product basis convention.** If $(e_{a})_{a\in\mathbf A}$ is a finite or
countable orthonormal basis of $H$ and $(f_{b})_{b\in\mathbf B}$ one of $K$,
then $(\kappa(e_{a}\otimes f_{b}))_{(a,b)\in\mathbf A\times\mathbf B}$ is an
orthonormal basis of $H\widehat\otimes K$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]] clause (d)); every
$\Psi\in H\widehat\otimes K$ has the expansion
$$\Psi=\sum_{a,b}c_{ab}\,\kappa(e_{a}\otimes f_{b}),\qquad c_{ab}\in\mathbb C,$$
converging in norm. A **product vector** is $\kappa(u\otimes v)$ for
$u\in H$, $v\in K$, and a **product preparation** is a state of the form
$T_{\Psi,\Psi}$ with $\Psi=\kappa(u\otimes v)$, $\|u\|=\|v\|=1$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]). General composite
preparations are linear superpositions and mixtures of product preparations
and need not factor; this is clause (iv) of P1.

**(c) Local readout of an assigned sharp observable.** Let $(A,u_{A})$ be an
assigned sharp observable of subsystem $A$ with spectral projection valued
measure $E_{A}$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$
([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clauses (a),
(b), the spectral measure being regular by
[[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]]). Define
$$F_{A}(B):=E_{A}(B)\otimes I_{K}\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}) .$$
By [[lem-nrqm-composites-local-pvm-tensor-extension]] clauses (a) and (d),
$F_{A}$ is a regular projection valued measure on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra
of $\mathbb R$ acting on $H\widehat\otimes K$
([[def-projection-valued-measure]]). Its integral
$A^{\mathrm{loc}}:=\int\lambda\,dF_{A}$ with domain
$\{\Psi:\int\lambda^{2}\,dF_{A,\Psi}(\lambda)<\infty\}$ is self-adjoint with
spectral projection valued measure $F_{A}$ by the converse direction of
[[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]]. The pair
$$(A^{\mathrm{loc}},u_{A})$$
is therefore an assigned sharp observable of the composite
([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (a)); it
is the **local readout of $(A,u_{A})$ on the declared composite**, and the unit
$u_{A}$ is read as before ([[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]). Its
outcome law in a preparation $\rho\in D(H\widehat\otimes K)$ is
$$\mu^{A^{\mathrm{loc}}}_{\rho}(B)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,(E_{A}(B)\otimes I_{K})\bigr) .$$
The analogous construction with the roles of $A$ and $B$ exchanged gives the
local readout of an assigned sharp observable of $B$.

**(d) Local effects.** A **local effect** of subsystem $A$ is a bounded
operator of the form $F\otimes I_{K}$ with $0\le F\le I_{H}$ in the
quadratic-form order; the map $F\mapsto F\otimes I_{K}$ is well defined by
[[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]] clause (a), and $F\otimes I_{K}$
is an effect on $H\widehat\otimes K$: it is bounded, self-adjoint
$((F\otimes I)^{*}=F^{*}\otimes I=F\otimes I)$, and it factors as
$$F\otimes I_{K}=\bigl(F^{1/2}\otimes I_{K}\bigr)^{*}\bigl(F^{1/2}\otimes I_{K}\bigr),\qquad I_{H}\otimes I_{K}-F\otimes I_{K}=\bigl((I-F)^{1/2}\otimes I_{K}\bigr)^{*}\bigl((I-F)^{1/2}\otimes I_{K}\bigr),$$
with the positive square roots of the continuous functional calculus
([[thm-continuous-functional-calculus-for-bounded-self-adjoint-operators]]) and
the product and adjoint rules of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]] clauses (b), (c); hence
$0\le F\otimes I_{K}\le I_{H}\otimes I_{K}$ in the quadratic-form order
([[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]], [[def-bounded-linear-operator]]).
Local effects of subsystem $B$ are defined in the same way.

**(e) Local instruments.** Let $(M_{a,r})_{\substack{a\in A\\r\in R_{a}}}$ be a
declared finite or countable instrument of subsystem $A$ with Kraus family as
in [[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]]
clause (d), normalized in the strong sense
$\sum_{a,r}M_{a,r}^{*}M_{a,r}=I_{H}$. The **local extension** of the instrument
to the declared composite is the family
$$\bigl(M_{a,r}\otimes I_{K}\bigr)_{\substack{a\in A\\r\in R_{a}}}$$
together with the outcome effects $\sum_{r}(M_{a,r}\otimes I_{K})^{*}(M_{a,r}\otimes I_{K})=\bigl(\sum_{r}M_{a,r}^{*}M_{a,r}\bigr)\otimes I_{K}$
and the conditional updates
$$\rho\longmapsto\frac{1}{p_{a}}\sum_{r}(M_{a,r}\otimes I_{K})\,\rho\,(M_{a,r}\otimes I_{K})^{*},\qquad p_{a}=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,F_{a}^{\mathrm{loc}}\bigr).$$
It is normalized: every finite partial sum of
$\sum_{a,r}(M_{a,r}\otimes I_{K})^{*}(M_{a,r}\otimes I_{K})$ equals
$\bigl(\sum_{a\le N,r\le R}M_{a,r}^{*}M_{a,r}\bigr)\otimes I_{K}$ by linearity
of tensoring with $I_{K}$, the finite partial sums
$\sum_{a\le N,r\le R}M_{a,r}^{*}M_{a,r}$ are uniformly bounded by $I_{H}$ and
converge strongly to $I_{H}$, so clause (c) of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-local-pvm-tensor-extension]] gives strong convergence of
the extended partial sums to $I_{H}\otimes I_{K}$; hence the local extension is
a declared finite or countable instrument of the composite in the sense of
clause (d) of
[[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]]. The
same construction applies with the roles of $A$ and $B$ exchanged.

**(f) Scope.** Clauses (a)-(e) fix the reading of clause (iv) of P1 together
with clauses (i), (ii) and (iv) of P2 and clause (v) of P3 for a declared pair
of distinguishable subsystems. They add no physical assumption to those
postulates beyond the readings displayed. In particular: the subsystems are
distinguishable, so no exchange sector, symmetrization or exclusion statement
is introduced (those are separate assumptions of P6); no superselection
restriction or algebraic replacement of the tensor product is adopted; no
interaction, dynamics, disturbance of the other subsystem or correlation is
asserted; and whether a concrete laboratory arrangement realizes a declared
composite, a declared local readout or a declared local instrument is a tested
identification with uncertainty under P7, not a consequence of this
definition.

## Remarks

- **Why the local readout is constructed through the spectral measure.** The
  composite operator $A\otimes I_{K}$ for an unbounded assigned observable $A$
  is not defined by this page directly; the local readout is defined through
  its spectral projection valued measure $E_{A}(\cdot)\otimes I_{K}$, whose
  regularity is supplied by
  [[lem-nrqm-composites-local-pvm-tensor-extension]] clause (d). For a bounded
  $A$ the local readout coincides with the bounded operator $A\otimes I_{K}$
  of [[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]] clause (a): both have the same
  spectral measure, since $A=\int\lambda\,dE_{A}$ and
  $A\otimes I_{K}=\int\lambda\,d(E_{A}\otimes I_{K})$ by clause (b) of the
  lemma, so the two self-adjoint operators agree by uniqueness of the spectral
  measure.
- **Choice hypotheses.** The tensor construction uses Countable Choice; the
  spectral measure of an assigned sharp observable and its converse use the
  Axiom of Choice. Both are carried as stated and are inherited by the results
  of this page that invoke the local readout.

items.title: Reduced preparations of a declared composite: the subsystem states of the framework
items.statement:
## Definition

Adopt the declared composite model of
[[def-nrqm-composites-framework-composite-systems-and-local-readouts]] with
subsystems $A,B$, assigned spaces $H,K$ and composite space
$H\widehat\otimes K$, the state postulate P1
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]]) and the state space
$D(H\widehat\otimes K)$ of the framework
([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]). Assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), the hypothesis of the cited
partial-trace and tensor construction results. The following vocabulary is
used by this page.

**(a) Reduced preparations.** For a preparation $\rho\in
D(H\widehat\otimes K)$ of the declared composite, the **reduced preparation
of subsystem $A$** is
$$\rho_{A}:=\operatorname{Tr}_{K}\rho\in D(H),$$
the image of $\rho$ under the partial trace $\operatorname{Tr}_{K}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-separable-partial-trace]] clause (a), characterized by
$$\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{A}X)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,(X\otimes I_{K})\bigr) \qquad\text{for every bounded }X\in\mathcal B(H);$$
the **reduced preparation of subsystem $B$** is
$\rho_{B}:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H}\rho\in D(K)$, characterized by
$\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{B}Y)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho\,(I_{H}\otimes Y))$ for
every bounded $Y\in\mathcal B(K)$. By clause (b) of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-separable-partial-trace]] the partial trace maps density
operators to density operators and is trace preserving, so $\rho_{A}$ and
$\rho_{B}$ are states of the respective subsystems in the sense of the state
space of the framework.

**(b) Affineness and continuity.** The maps $\rho\mapsto\rho_{A}$ and
$\rho\mapsto\rho_{B}$ are affine and continuous in the trace norm:
$\operatorname{Tr}_{K}$ is linear and $\|\operatorname{Tr}_{K}T\|_{1}\le\|T\|_{1}$
by clause (a) of [[lem-nrqm-composites-separable-partial-trace]], with the
trace norm of [[thm-trace-class-is-a-two-sided-banach-operator-ideal]]. In
particular the reduction of a statistical mixture
$\sum_{n}w_{n}\rho_{n}\in D(H\widehat\otimes K)$ of composite preparations is
the corresponding mixture $\sum_{n}w_{n}\rho_{A,n}$ of the reduced
preparations.

**(c) Product preparations reduce to their factors.** If
$\Psi=\kappa(u\otimes v)$ with $\|u\|=\|v\|=1$ and $\rho=T_{\Psi,\Psi}$ is a
product preparation ([[def-nrqm-composites-framework-composite-systems-and-local-readouts]]
clause (b), [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]), then
$$T_{u\otimes v,\,u\otimes v}=T_{u,u}\otimes T_{v,v}$$
as bounded operators on $H\widehat\otimes K$, because both sides agree on
every elementary tensor $\kappa(x\otimes y)$ in the sense of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]] clause (a) and $\kappa[H\odot K]$
is dense ([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]] clause (c));
consequently
$$\rho_{A}=T_{u,u},\qquad \rho_{B}=T_{v,v}$$
by clause (c) of [[lem-nrqm-composites-separable-partial-trace]]. Thus a
product preparation is exactly a preparation whose reductions reconstruct it,
$\rho=\rho_{A}\otimes\rho_{B}$, and whose reductions are pure.

**(d) Correlated and uncorrelated preparations.** A composite preparation
$\rho$ is called **uncorrelated** when $\rho=\rho_{A}\otimes\rho_{B}$ and
**correlated** otherwise; a pure preparation
$T_{\Psi,\Psi}$ is called a product preparation when $\Psi$ is a product
vector and **non-product** otherwise
([[def-nrqm-composites-separable-and-entangled-states]] clauses (a), (b)).
These are descriptive names for the displayed algebraic conditions; the
statistical reading of the distinction, including the failure of
factorization of local outcome laws for non-product pure preparations, is a
theorem of this page and is not assumed here.

**(e) Status.** Clauses (a)-(d) fix vocabulary: the subsystem states attached
to a composite preparation by the partial trace. The reduction is a
mathematical operation on the model description. It is not a dynamics, not an
interaction, not a measurement and not a physical discarding of subsystem $B$;
no disturbance of either subsystem and no empirical fact is asserted, and the
question whether a laboratory procedure prepares a state whose reduction is a
prescribed state is a tested identification with uncertainty under P7. The
physical reading of clause (a) — that the reduced preparation reproduces every
local outcome law of subsystem $A$ — is a theorem of this page and is not
assumed here.

items.title: Schmidt reduction of a pure composite preparation, purity of the subsystems, and the product criterion
items.statement:
## Statement

Adopt the framework's composition and state readings for a declared composite
of two distinguishable subsystems $A,B$ with assigned spaces $H,K$
([[def-nrqm-composites-framework-composite-systems-and-local-readouts]],
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]],
[[def-nrqm-composites-framework-reduced-preparations]]), and assume the Axiom
of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), the hypothesis of the cited
mathematical suppliers. Let $\Psi\in H\widehat\otimes K$ satisfy
$\|\Psi\|=1$, let
$$\rho=T_{\Psi,\Psi}\in D(H\widehat\otimes K),\qquad \rho_{A}=\operatorname{Tr}_{K}\rho\in D(H),\qquad \rho_{B}=\operatorname{Tr}_{H}\rho\in D(K)$$
be the pure preparation of the declared composite and its two reduced
preparations. Then:

**(a) Schmidt expansion and reductions.** There are an at most countable index
set $J$, orthonormal families $(v_{r})_{r\in J}\subseteq H$,
$(u_{r})_{r\in J}\subseteq K$ and numbers $s_{r}>0$ with
$$\Psi=\sum_{r\in J}s_{r}\,\kappa(v_{r}\otimes u_{r})\quad\text{(norm convergence)},\qquad \sum_{r\in J}s_{r}^{2}=1,$$
and the reduced preparations are given by the trace-norm convergent series
$$\rho_{A}=\sum_{r\in J}s_{r}^{2}\,T_{v_{r},v_{r}},\qquad \rho_{B}=\sum_{r\in J}s_{r}^{2}\,T_{u_{r},u_{r}} .$$
Moreover $\operatorname{tr}\rho_{A}^{2}=\operatorname{tr}\rho_{B}^{2}=\sum_{r\in J}s_{r}^{4}$.

**(b) Purity and product criterion.** The following are equivalent:
(i) exactly one $s_{r}$ is nonzero; (ii) $\rho_{A}$ is pure, that is
$\operatorname{tr}\rho_{A}^{2}=1$; (iii) $\rho_{B}$ is pure;
(iv) $\Psi$ is a product vector, $\Psi=\kappa(u\otimes v)$ with
$\|u\|=\|v\|=1$; (v) $\rho=\rho_{A}\otimes\rho_{B}$; (vi) $\rho$ is separable in the trace-norm closed-convex-hull sense of [[def-nrqm-composites-separable-and-entangled-states]] clause (b). In that case
$s_{r_{0}}=1$ at the unique nonzero index and $\Psi=\kappa(v_{r_{0}}\otimes u_{r_{0}})$,
$\rho_{A}=T_{u,u}$, $\rho_{B}=T_{v,v}$ for $u=v_{r_{0}}$, $v=u_{r_{0}}$.

**(c) Non-product pure preparations.** If $\Psi$ is not a product vector, then
at least two coefficients $s_{r}$ are nonzero, $\rho_{A}$ and $\rho_{B}$ are
mixed, $\operatorname{tr}\rho_{A}^{2}<1$, and $\rho\ne\rho_{A}\otimes\rho_{B}$;
the pure preparation is entangled in the full trace-norm closed-convex-hull sense of [[def-nrqm-composites-separable-and-entangled-states]] clause (b). More precisely, if $m=\max_rs_r^2<1$, every separable $\sigma$ satisfies $\operatorname{tr}(\sigma\rho)\le m$ and $\|\rho-\sigma\|_1\ge1-m>0$.

**(d) Scope.** The statement concerns the declared composite, its pure
preparations and the reduced preparations of the factors. It asserts no
dynamics, no interaction, no measurement, no apparatus realization and no
empirical fact; and it concerns pure composite preparations only, mixed-state
separability being outside its scope.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The declared composite with assigned spaces $H,K$; a unit vector $\Psi\in H\widehat\otimes K$; the preparations $\rho,\rho_{A},\rho_{B}$; the Axiom of Countable Choice.

[F1] **Schmidt expansion.** For $\Psi\in H\widehat\otimes K$ there are an at most countable $J$, orthonormal families $(v_{r})\subseteq H$, $(u_{r})\subseteq K$ and $s_{r}>0$ with $\Psi=\sum_{r}s_{r}\kappa(v_{r}\otimes u_{r})$ in norm, $\|\Psi\|^{2}=\sum_{r}s_{r}^{2}$; the $s_{r}$ are the positive square roots of the nonzero eigenvalues of the coefficient operator on countable factor supports; and for $\|\Psi\|=1$ the reduced density $\rho=\operatorname{Tr}_{K}T_{\Psi,\Psi}$ satisfies $\operatorname{tr}\rho^{2}=\sum_{r}s_{r}^{4}$, with $\operatorname{tr}\rho^{2}=1$ exactly when exactly one $s_{r}$ is nonzero, i.e. exactly when $\Psi$ is a product vector ([[thm-nrqm-composites-infinite-schmidt-decomposition]]; the completed tensor product and the embedding $\kappa$ are those of [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]). For bounded $X\in\mathcal B(H)$ and $x,y\in H$ the tensor identity $(X\otimes I_{K})\kappa(x\otimes y)=\kappa(Xx\otimes y)$ holds ([[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]] clause (a)).

[F2] **Partial trace.** There is a linear positive trace-preserving map $\operatorname{Tr}_{K}$ on trace-class operators with $\operatorname{tr}((\operatorname{Tr}_{K}T)X)=\operatorname{tr}(T(X\otimes I_{K}))$ for every trace-class $T$ and every bounded $X\in\mathcal B(H)$ and $\|\operatorname{Tr}_{K}T\|_{1}\le\|T\|_{1}$; it maps density operators to density operators ([[lem-nrqm-composites-separable-partial-trace]] clauses (a), (b)); on rank-one operators $\operatorname{Tr}_{K}T_{u\otimes v,u'\otimes v'}=\langle v,v'\rangle T_{u,u'}$ (clause (c)).

[F3] **Rank-one trace pairing.** For trace-class $S$ and $x,y\in H$ one has $\operatorname{tr}(ST_{x,y})=\langle Sx,y\rangle$, and $T_{x,x}\ge0$ with $\operatorname{tr}T_{x,x}=\|x\|^{2}$, $T_{x,y}$ being bounded with $\|T_{x,y}\|=\|x\|\,\|y\|$; the map $(x,y)\mapsto T_{x,y}$ is trace-norm continuous ([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]] clauses (a), (b), (c), (e), (f), [[thm-trace-class-is-a-two-sided-banach-operator-ideal]]).

[F4] **Purity criterion.** A state is pure exactly when its purity $\operatorname{tr}\rho^{2}$ equals one ([[lem-nrqm-state-geometry-purity-criterion]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a)).

[F5] **Reduced preparations and product preparations.** $\rho_{A}=\operatorname{Tr}_{K}\rho$ and $\rho_{B}=\operatorname{Tr}_{H}\rho$ are the reduced preparations of the declared composite, and for a product preparation $T_{\kappa(u\otimes v),\kappa(u\otimes v)}=T_{u,u}\otimes T_{v,v}$, so that $\rho_{A}=T_{u,u}$ and $\rho_{B}=T_{v,v}$ ([[def-nrqm-composites-framework-reduced-preparations]] clauses (a), (c), [[def-nrqm-composites-framework-composite-systems-and-local-readouts]] clause (b)).

[F6] The mathematical equivalence of a pure projector being separable with its vector being product, and the strict Schmidt-overlap/trace-norm witness for non-product vectors, are [[lem-nrqm-composites-pure-state-separability-criterion]]. Its closed convex hull is exactly the one declared in the definition.

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; obtain the Schmidt expansion from the infinite
Schmidt theorem, pass the partial trace identity to the trace-norm limit
through finite truncations to identify the two reduced preparations, and read
off the purity and product criteria from the supplier's purity statement and
the purity criterion for states.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F5].

1.1 [Expansion and normalization] By [F1] there are $J$, $(v_{r})$, $(u_{r})$ and $s_{r}>0$ with $\Psi=\sum_{r}s_{r}\kappa(v_{r}\otimes u_{r})$ in norm and $\sum_{r}s_{r}^{2}=\|\Psi\|^{2}=1$; this is the expansion of (a). [given, F1]

1.2 [Finite truncations] Put $\Psi_{N}:=\sum_{r\in J_{N}}s_{r}\kappa(v_{r}\otimes u_{r})$ for an increasing sequence of finite subsets $J_{N}\uparrow J$. For bounded $X\in\mathcal B(H)$ and $N$ one has, using the tensor identity of [F1] on elementary tensors, $\langle(X\otimes I_{K})\Psi_{N},\Psi_{N}\rangle=\sum_{r,r'\in J_{N}}s_{r}s_{r'}\langle Xv_{r},v_{r'}\rangle\langle u_{r},u_{r'}\rangle=\sum_{r\in J_{N}}s_{r}^{2}\langle Xv_{r},v_{r}\rangle$ by orthonormality of $(u_{r})$; since $\Psi_{N}\to\Psi$, $\|X\otimes I_{K}\|\le\|X\|$ and $\sum_{r}s_{r}^{2}<\infty$, the sesquilinear form is continuous and the series converges absolutely, so $\operatorname{tr}(\rho(X\otimes I_{K}))=\langle(X\otimes I_{K})\Psi,\Psi\rangle=\sum_{r}s_{r}^{2}\langle Xv_{r},v_{r}\rangle$. [given, F1, F3, algebra]

2.1 [Reduction identity] Let $S:=\sum_{r}s_{r}^{2}T_{v_{r},v_{r}}$, a trace-class operator with $S\ge0$ and $\operatorname{tr}S=1$ by [F3] and absolute convergence. For bounded $X$, step 1.2 and [F2] give $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{A}X)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho(X\otimes I_{K}))=\sum_{r}s_{r}^{2}\langle Xv_{r},v_{r}\rangle$; taking $X=T_{w,w'}$ and using [F3] twice, $\langle\rho_{A}w,w'\rangle=\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{A}T_{w,w'})=\sum_{r}s_{r}^{2}\langle T_{w,w'}v_{r},v_{r}\rangle=\sum_{r}s_{r}^{2}\langle v_{r},w'\rangle\langle w,v_{r}\rangle=\langle Sw,w'\rangle$ for all $w,w'\in H$, so $\rho_{A}=S$ by taking $w'=(\rho_{A}-S)w$ and using $\|(\rho_{A}-S)w\|^{2}=0$; interchanging the factors gives $\rho_{B}=\sum_{r}s_{r}^{2}T_{u_{r},u_{r}}$ with the same argument. [given, F2, F3, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 [Purity and product criterion] By [F1] and step 2.1, $\operatorname{tr}\rho_{A}^{2}=\sum_{r}s_{r}^{4}=\operatorname{tr}\rho_{B}^{2}$ and $\operatorname{tr}\rho_{A}^{2}=1$ holds exactly when exactly one $s_{r}$ is nonzero and exactly when $\Psi$ is a product vector; purity of $\rho_{A}$ is equivalent to $\operatorname{tr}\rho_{A}^{2}=1$ by [F4], and likewise for $\rho_{B}$. If exactly one $s_{r_{0}}$ is nonzero, then $s_{r_{0}}^{2}=1$ and $\Psi=\kappa(v_{r_{0}}\otimes u_{r_{0}})$ is a product vector, so $\rho=\rho_{A}\otimes\rho_{B}$ by [F5]; conversely for a product vector [F5] gives $\rho_{A}=T_{u,u}$, $\rho_{B}=T_{v,v}$, which are pure by [F3] and [F4]. This is (b); its failure case, in which at least two $s_{r}$ are nonzero and both reduced preparations are mixed with $\operatorname{tr}\rho_{A}^{2}<1$ and $\rho\ne\rho_{A}\otimes\rho_{B}$, is (c). Conversely, if $\rho=\rho_A\otimes\rho_B$, pair both operators with the unit product vector $q_r=\kappa(v_r\otimes u_r)$. The expansion gives $\langle\rho q_r,q_r\rangle=s_r^2$, while step 2.1 and the tensor action in [F1] give $\langle(\rho_A\otimes\rho_B)q_r,q_r\rangle=s_r^4$. Thus every positive $s_r^2$ equals its square and is one; their sum one forces exactly one coefficient. Finally [F6] identifies this product case exactly with separability, proving (vi); in the non-product case it gives entanglement and the stated strict trace-norm witness. [given, F1, F4, F5, F6, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 [Assembly and scope] Step 1.1 gives the expansion of (a) and step 2.1 its reduction formulae; step 3.1 establishes (b) and (c); only the declared composite, its pure preparations and the cited mathematics were used, which is the scope statement (d). [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1] ∎

## Remarks

- **Pure versus mixed scope.** Clause (c) proves non-product pure preparations entangled for the full trace-norm closed convex hull. A general classification or criterion for mixed-state separability is not claimed.
- **Choice.** Only the Axiom of Countable Choice is used, through the tensor
  construction and the Schmidt theorem; no spectral theorem for unbounded
  operators enters this item.

items.title: Local readout laws and reduced preparations: the subsystem state determines, and is determined by, the local statistics
items.statement:
## Statement

Adopt the framework's composition, state and measurement readings for a
declared composite of two distinguishable subsystems $A,B$ with assigned
spaces $H,K$ ([[def-nrqm-composites-framework-composite-systems-and-local-readouts]],
[[def-nrqm-composites-framework-reduced-preparations]],
[[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]]),
and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of
the cited suppliers. Let $\rho,\rho'\in D(H\widehat\otimes K)$ be
preparations with reduced preparations $\rho_{A}=\operatorname{Tr}_{K}\rho$,
$\rho'_{A}=\operatorname{Tr}_{K}\rho'$ and
$\rho_{B}=\operatorname{Tr}_{H}\rho$. Then:

**(a) Local readout law.** For every assigned sharp observable $(A,u_{A})$ of
subsystem $A$ with local readout $(A^{\mathrm{loc}},u_{A})$ and every Borel
$B\subseteq\mathbb R$,
$$\mu^{A^{\mathrm{loc}}}_{\rho}(B)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,(E_{A}(B)\otimes I_{K})\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho_{A}\,E_{A}(B)\bigr)=\mu^{A}_{\rho_{A}}(B),$$
where $E_{A}$ is the spectral projection valued measure of $A$. In particular
the local statistics of subsystem $A$ depend on the composite preparation only
through its reduced preparation, and if $\rho_{A}=\rho'_{A}$ then every local
readout law is the same in $\rho$ and in $\rho'$.

**(b) Determination of the reduced preparation.** Conversely, if
$\rho_{A}\ne\rho'_{A}$, then there are a bounded assigned sharp observable
$(P,1)$ of subsystem $A$ and a Borel set $B$ with
$\mu^{P^{\mathrm{loc}}}_{\rho}(B)\ne\mu^{P^{\mathrm{loc}}}_{\rho'}(B)$: the
family of local readout laws of subsystem $A$ determines $\rho_{A}$ among the
preparations of the composite.

**(c) Ideal local measurement.** Let $(P_{a})_{a\in A_{0}}$ be a declared
ideal sharp measurement of subsystem $A$
([[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]]
clause (a)). Then $(P_{a}\otimes I_{K})_{a\in A_{0}}$ is a declared ideal
sharp measurement of the declared composite, its outcome probabilities in a
preparation $\rho$ are
$$p_{a}=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,(P_{a}\otimes I_{K})\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{A}P_{a}),$$
and for $p_{a}>0$ the conditional state
$\rho_{a}:=(P_{a}\otimes I_{K})\rho\,(P_{a}\otimes I_{K})/p_{a}$ of the
composite has the reduced preparation
$$(\rho_{a})_{A}=\frac{P_{a}\rho_{A}P_{a}}{p_{a}},$$
which is the selective Lueders update of $\rho_{A}$ by $P_{a}$. The
discarded-outcome state $\Phi(\rho)=\sum_{a}(P_{a}\otimes I_{K})\rho\,(P_{a}\otimes I_{K})$
has reduced preparations
$$\Phi(\rho)_{A}=\sum_{a}P_{a}\rho_{A}P_{a},\qquad \Phi(\rho)_{B}=\operatorname{Tr}_{H}\Phi(\rho)=\rho_{B} .$$
The analogous statements hold with the roles of $A$ and $B$ exchanged.

**(d) Scope.** Clauses (a)-(c) are conditional consequences of P1, P2 and P3
in the readings of the cited items and of the cited mathematics. They concern
the declared composite and its declared measurements; they assert no dynamics,
no interaction, no apparatus realization, no uniqueness of recorded outcomes
and no empirical fact, and clause (c) is a statement about the declared ideal
Lueders instrument only, not about every laboratory procedure.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The declared composite with assigned spaces $H,K$; preparations $\rho,\rho'$; reduced preparations $\rho_{A},\rho'_{A},\rho_{B}$; an assigned sharp observable $(A,u_{A})$ of subsystem $A$ with spectral measure $E_{A}$; a declared ideal sharp measurement $(P_{a})_{a\in A_{0}}$ of subsystem $A$; the choice hypotheses.

[F1] **Local readout and its outcome law.** For an assigned sharp observable $(A,u_{A})$ of subsystem $A$, the local readout $(A^{\mathrm{loc}},u_{A})$ is the assigned sharp observable of the composite with spectral projection valued measure $F_{A}=E_{A}(\cdot)\otimes I_{K}$, so that $\mu^{A^{\mathrm{loc}}}_{\rho}(B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho(E_{A}(B)\otimes I_{K}))$; $E_{A}$ is regular and $F_{A}$ is a regular projection valued measure by [[lem-nrqm-composites-local-pvm-tensor-extension]] ([[def-nrqm-composites-framework-composite-systems-and-local-readouts]] clause (c), [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clauses (a), (b)).

[F2] **Partial trace.** $\operatorname{tr}((\operatorname{Tr}_{K}T)X)=\operatorname{tr}(T(X\otimes I_{K}))$ for every trace-class $T$ and bounded $X$, and $\operatorname{Tr}_{K}$ is linear, positive, trace preserving and trace-norm contractive; moreover $\operatorname{Tr}_{K}T_{u\otimes v,u'\otimes v'}=\langle v,v'\rangle T_{u,u'}$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-separable-partial-trace]] clauses (a), (b), (c)).

[F3] **Trace pairing and cyclicity.** For trace-class $T$ and bounded $B$ one has $\operatorname{tr}(BT)=\operatorname{tr}(TB)$ and $|\operatorname{tr}T|\le\|T\|_{1}$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-nuclear-bounded-cyclicity]] clause (b), [[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]], [[thm-trace-class-is-a-two-sided-banach-operator-ideal]] clauses 1, 2); the rank-one operators satisfy $\operatorname{tr}(ST_{w,w'})=\langle Sw,w'\rangle$, $T_{w,w'}$ is bounded with $\|T_{w,w'}\|=\|w\|\,\|w'\|$, and $T_{w,w}$ is an orthogonal projection for unit $w$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]] clauses (a), (b), (c), (e)).

[F4] **Separating local statistics.** If two density operators $\rho_{A}\ne\rho'_{A}$ on $H$ are distinct, then there is a unit $w$ with $\langle\rho_{A}w,w\rangle\ne\langle\rho'_{A}w,w\rangle$, and the rank-one projection $P=T_{w,w}$ has the outcome laws $\mu^{P}_{\rho_{A}}(\{1\})=\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{A}P)=\langle\rho_{A}w,w\rangle$ and $\mu^{P}_{\rho'_{A}}(\{1\})=\langle\rho'_{A}w,w\rangle$ ([[lem-nrqm-observables-states-separated-by-bounded-projections]] clauses (a), (b), [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (b)).

[F5] **Ideal sharp measurement of the composite.** For a declared ideal sharp measurement $(P_{a})$ of a system, the outcome probability in $\rho$ is $p_{a}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_{a})$, the conditional state is $P_{a}\rho P_{a}/p_{a}$ when $p_{a}>0$, and the discarded-outcome state is the trace-norm convergent sum $\Phi(\rho)=\sum_{a}P_{a}\rho P_{a}$ with $\operatorname{tr}(\Phi(\rho)P_{a})=p_{a}$ ([[pthm-nrqm-measurement-projective-outcomes-and-discarded-ensembles]] clauses (a), (b), (c), [[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]] clauses (a), (b)).

[F6] **Tensor calculus and strong continuity.** $(S\otimes I_{K})\kappa(x\otimes y)=\kappa(Sx\otimes y)$ for bounded $S$, and $(S\otimes T)(S'\otimes T')=(SS')\otimes(TT')$, $(S\otimes T)^{*}=S^{*}\otimes T^{*}$, $\|S\otimes T\|\le\|S\|\,\|T\|$ for bounded operators ([[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]] clauses (a), (b), (c)); if a sequence of bounded operators is uniformly bounded and converges strongly, then tensoring with $I_{K}$ preserves the strong convergence ([[lem-nrqm-composites-local-pvm-tensor-extension]] clause (c)).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; establish the intertwining identity for the partial
trace and bounded operators on one factor, derive the local readout law from
the partial trace characterization, read the determination of the reduced
preparation off the separating rank-one projection, and compute the conditional
and discarded reductions of a local ideal sharp measurement with the
intertwining identity.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F6].

1.1 [Intertwining identity] Let $T$ be trace class on $H\widehat\otimes K$ and $X,Y$ bounded on $H$. For every bounded $Z$ on $H$, [F2] gives $\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\operatorname{Tr}_{K}\bigl((X\otimes I)T(Y\otimes I)\bigr)Z\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl((X\otimes I)T(Y\otimes I)(Z\otimes I)\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(T(YZX\otimes I)\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl((\operatorname{Tr}_{K}T)(YZX)\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(X(\operatorname{Tr}_{K}T)YZ\bigr)$ by [F3] and [F6]; since $\operatorname{Tr}_{K}((X\otimes I)T(Y\otimes I))$ and $X(\operatorname{Tr}_{K}T)Y$ are trace-class operators with equal trace pairings against every bounded $Z$, they are equal by [F3]. [F2, F3, F6, algebra]

1.2 [The extended family is a declared measurement] The operators $P_{a}\otimes I_{K}$ are orthogonal projections by [F6]; $P_{a}P_{b}=0$ for $a\ne b$ gives $(P_{a}\otimes I_{K})(P_{b}\otimes I_{K})=(P_{a}P_{b})\otimes I_{K}=0$; and $\sum_{a\in A_{0}}(P_{a}\otimes I_{K})=I_{H}\otimes I_{K}$ in the strong sense, because the finite partial sums are $(\sum_{a\le N}P_{a})\otimes I_{K}$ by linearity and converge strongly to $I_{H}\otimes I_{K}$ by [F6], the projections $\sum_{a\le N}P_{a}$ being uniformly bounded and converging strongly to $I_{H}$. Hence $(P_{a}\otimes I_{K})$ is a declared ideal sharp measurement of the composite. [given, F6, algebra]

1.3 [Local readout law] For every Borel $B$, [F1] gives $\mu^{A^{\mathrm{loc}}}_{\rho}(B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho(E_{A}(B)\otimes I_{K}))$, and [F2] applied with the bounded operator $E_{A}(B)$ gives $\operatorname{tr}(\rho(E_{A}(B)\otimes I_{K}))=\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{A}E_{A}(B))=\mu^{A}_{\rho_{A}}(B)$ by [F1]; applying the same identity to $\rho'$ gives the case $\rho_{A}=\rho'_{A}$, so this is (a). [given, F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 [Determination of the reduced preparation] Suppose $\rho_{A}\ne\rho'_{A}$. By [F4] there is a unit $w$ with $\langle\rho_{A}w,w\rangle\ne\langle\rho'_{A}w,w\rangle$; declare the bounded self-adjoint operator $P:=T_{w,w}$ with unit $1$ as a bounded assigned sharp observable of subsystem $A$. Its local readout $(P^{\mathrm{loc}},1)$ has, by step 1.3, the outcome law $\mu^{P^{\mathrm{loc}}}_{\rho}(\{1\})=\operatorname{tr}(\rho(P\otimes I_{K}))=\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{A}P)=\langle\rho_{A}w,w\rangle$, and likewise $\mu^{P^{\mathrm{loc}}}_{\rho'}(\{1\})=\langle\rho'_{A}w,w\rangle$; the two numbers differ, so some local readout law differs, which is (b). [given, F3, F4, step 1.3, algebra]

2.2 [Conditional local measurement] By step 1.2 the family $(P_{a}\otimes I_{K})$ is a declared ideal sharp measurement of the composite, so [F5] gives $p_{a}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho(P_{a}\otimes I_{K}))=\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{A}P_{a})$ by [F2], and the conditional state $\rho_{a}=(P_{a}\otimes I_{K})\rho(P_{a}\otimes I_{K})/p_{a}$ for $p_{a}>0$. Step 1.1 with $X=Y=P_{a}$ gives $\operatorname{Tr}_{K}\bigl((P_{a}\otimes I_{K})\rho(P_{a}\otimes I_{K})\bigr)=P_{a}\rho_{A}P_{a}$, hence $(\rho_{a})_{A}=P_{a}\rho_{A}P_{a}/p_{a}$; the conditional update of the composite reduces to the selective Lueders update of $\rho_{A}$, which is the first part of (c). [given, F2, F5, step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra]

2.3 [Discarded local measurement] The discarded-outcome state $\Phi(\rho)$ of [F5] has $A$-reduction $\sum_{a}P_{a}\rho_{A}P_{a}$: apply $\operatorname{Tr}_{K}$ to the trace-norm convergent series termwise using step 1.1 and the trace-norm continuity of $\operatorname{Tr}_{K}$ from [F2]. For the $B$-reduction let $Y$ be bounded on $K$; then $\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\operatorname{Tr}_{H}\Phi(\rho)Y\bigr)=\sum_{a}\operatorname{tr}\bigl((P_{a}\otimes I_{K})\rho(P_{a}\otimes I_{K})(I_{H}\otimes Y)\bigr)=\sum_{a}\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho(P_{a}\otimes Y)\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\bigl(\sum_{a}P_{a}\otimes Y\bigr)\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho(I_{H}\otimes Y)\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{B}Y)$ by [F2], [F3] and [F6], using the strong convergence of $\sum_{a\le N}P_{a}\otimes Y$ to $I_{H}\otimes Y$ and $|\operatorname{tr}(\rho A)|\le\|\rho\|_{1}\|A\|$; since both sides are trace class with equal pairings against every bounded $Y$, they are equal. This completes (c); the exchanged-roles statement is the same argument with $H$ and $K$ interchanged. [given, F2, F3, F5, F6, step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 [Assembly and scope] Step 1.3 is (a), step 2.1 is (b), steps 2.2 and 2.3 are (c), and (d) records that only P1, P2, P3 in their stated readings and the cited mathematics were used. [step 1.3, step 2.1, step 2.2, step 2.3] ∎

## Remarks

- **Which factor is measured.** Clause (c) measures subsystem $A$; its
  discarded version leaves $\rho_{B}$ fixed while changing $\rho_{A}$ into the
  Lueders mixture. The conditional version changes the description of $B$ as
  well, and that conditional change is exactly the correlation between the
  factors; no signalling claim beyond the outcome-law invariance is made here.
- **Unbounded readouts.** Clause (a) covers unbounded assigned sharp
  observables of the factor, including the position and momentum observables of
  the massive-particle model, because the local readout is defined through the
  spectral measure $E_{A}(\cdot)\otimes I_{K}$.

The statement asserts no dynamics, no interaction, no disturbance of the other factor's statistics under the discarded measurement, no apparatus realization and no empirical fact; it is a conditional consequence of P2, P3 and the cited mathematics.

items.title: Factorization of local statistics for product preparations, and its failure for non-product pure preparations
items.statement:
## Statement

Adopt the framework's composition and state readings for a declared composite
of two distinguishable subsystems $A,B$ with assigned spaces $H,K$
([[def-nrqm-composites-framework-composite-systems-and-local-readouts]],
[[def-nrqm-composites-framework-reduced-preparations]]), and assume the Axiom
of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\Psi\in H\widehat\otimes K$
be a unit vector, $\rho=T_{\Psi,\Psi}$ the associated pure preparation, and
$\rho_{A}=\operatorname{Tr}_{K}\rho$, $\rho_{B}=\operatorname{Tr}_{H}\rho$ its
reduced preparations. Then:

**(a) Product preparations factorize.** If $\Psi=\kappa(u\otimes v)$ with
$\|u\|=\|v\|=1$, then for every bounded effect $F$ on $H$ and every bounded
effect $F'$ on $K$
$$\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,(F\otimes F')\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{A}F)\;\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{B}F').$$
In particular, for a declared finite-outcome measurement of $A$ with effect
family $(F_{i})$ and one of $B$ with $(F'_{j})$, the joint outcome
probabilities factorize, $p(i,j)=p_{A}(i)p_{B}(j)$: in a product preparation
the two subsystems have independent local statistics.

**(b) Non-product pure preparations are correlated.** If $\Psi$ is not a
product vector and
$\Psi=\sum_{r\in J}s_{r}\kappa(v_{r}\otimes u_{r})$ is its Schmidt expansion
with $s_{1}\ge s_{2}>0$, then the rank-one effects
$P:=T_{v_{1},v_{1}}$ on $H$ and $P':=T_{u_{2},u_{2}}$ on $K$ satisfy
$$\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,(P\otimes P')\bigr)=0\ \ne\ s_{1}^{2}s_{2}^{2}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{A}P)\;\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{B}P'),$$
so the joint law of the corresponding two-outcome local measurements does not
factorize; the product of the marginal probabilities exceeds the joint
probability by $s_{1}^{2}s_{2}^{2}>0$.

**(c) Scope.** The statement is a conditional computation for pure
preparations of the declared composite; it asserts no dynamics, no
interaction, no apparatus realization, no measured correlation and no
empirical fact, and it does not claim that a joint law failing to factorize
establishes any particular physical mechanism.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The declared composite with assigned spaces $H,K$; a unit vector $\Psi\in H\widehat\otimes K$; the preparations $\rho,\rho_{A},\rho_{B}$; bounded effects $F,F'$; the Schmidt expansion of $\Psi$ when it exists; the Axiom of Countable Choice.

[F1] **Schmidt reduction.** If $\Psi=\sum_{r}s_{r}\kappa(v_{r}\otimes u_{r})$ is the Schmidt expansion of [[thm-nrqm-composites-infinite-schmidt-decomposition]] with orthonormal families $(v_{r})$, $(u_{r})$ and $s_{r}>0$, $\sum_{r}s_{r}^{2}=1$, then $\rho_{A}=\sum_{r}s_{r}^{2}T_{v_{r},v_{r}}$ and $\rho_{B}=\sum_{r}s_{r}^{2}T_{u_{r},u_{r}}$; for a product vector $\Psi=\kappa(u\otimes v)$ one has $\rho_{A}=T_{u,u}$ and $\rho_{B}=T_{v,v}$ ([[pthm-nrqm-composites-schmidt-reduction-and-pure-entanglement]] clauses (a), (b), [[lem-nrqm-composites-separable-partial-trace]] clause (c)).

[F2] **Rank-one pairing.** For bounded $S$ and $w,w'\in H$ one has $\operatorname{tr}(T_{w,w}S)=\langle Sw,w\rangle$ and $T_{w,w}$ is an orthogonal projection for unit $w$; the same holds on $K$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]] clauses (c), (e), [[thm-trace-class-is-a-two-sided-banach-operator-ideal]] clause 2). Moreover for bounded $F$ and unit $\Psi$ the pairing $\operatorname{tr}(T_{\Psi,\Psi}F)=\langle F\Psi,\Psi\rangle=\|F^{1/2}\Psi\|^{2}\ge0$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (b)).

[F3] **Tensor calculus.** $(S\otimes S')\kappa(x\otimes y)=\kappa(Sx\otimes S'y)$ and $(S\otimes S')^{*}=S^{*}\otimes S'^{*}$, so $(F\otimes F')\kappa(x\otimes y)=\kappa(Fx\otimes F'y)$ for bounded $F,F'$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]] clauses (a), (c)); product vectors and the embedding $\kappa$ are those of [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]].

[F4] **Effects and finite-outcome measurements.** A declared finite-outcome measurement of a system has a finite family of bounded effects $0\le F_{i}\le I$ with $\sum_{i}F_{i}=I$ and outcome probabilities $\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_{i})$; for two subsystems the joint measurement of the local effects $F_{i}\otimes I_{K}$ and $I_{H}\otimes F'_{j}$ has outcome probabilities $\operatorname{tr}(\rho(F_{i}\otimes F'_{j}))$ ([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clauses (b), (f), [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] clauses (ii), (iv)).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; evaluate the joint pairing of elementary local
effects on a product preparation by the rank-one pairing, and on a non-product
preparation project onto the first Schmidt vector of one factor and the second
of the other.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F4].

1.1 [Product case] Let $\Psi=\kappa(u\otimes v)$ with $\|u\|=\|v\|=1$ and let $F,F'$ be bounded effects. By [F2] and [F3], $\operatorname{tr}(\rho(F\otimes F'))=\langle(F\otimes F')\Psi,\Psi\rangle_{\widehat\otimes}=\langle Fu,u\rangle_{H}\langle F'v,v\rangle_{K}=\operatorname{tr}(T_{u,u}F)\operatorname{tr}(T_{v,v}F')=\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{A}F)\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{B}F')$ by [F1], which is the identity of (a); the finite-outcome statement follows with the joint probabilities of [F4]. [given, F1, F2, F3, F4, algebra]

1.2 [Non-product case] Let $\Psi$ be non-product. By [F1] its norm-convergent Schmidt expansion has at least two positive coefficients; label two of them $s_{1}\ge s_{2}>0$ and put $P=T_{v_{1},v_{1}}$, $P'=T_{u_{2},u_{2}}$. Since $Pv_{r}=\delta_{r,1}v_{1}$ and $P'u_{r}=\delta_{r,2}u_{2}$ by the rank-one definition and orthonormality, [F3] gives $(P\otimes P')\kappa(v_{r}\otimes u_{r})=\delta_{r,1}\delta_{r,2}\kappa(v_{1}\otimes u_{2})=0$ for every $r$. Boundedness of $P\otimes P'$ passes this identity through the norm-convergent Schmidt expansion, so $(P\otimes P')\Psi=0$ and $\operatorname{tr}(\rho(P\otimes P'))=0$ by [F2]. The trace-norm expansions of the reduced preparations [F1], paired with the bounded projections, give $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{A}P)=s_{1}^{2}$ and $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{B}P')=s_{2}^{2}$ by [F2]. Thus the marginal product exceeds the joint probability by $s_{1}^{2}s_{2}^{2}>0$. The two local measurements $(P,I-P)$ and $(P',I-P')$ are effect families by [F2], [F4], and their $(+,+)$ entry already proves nonfactorization. [given, F1, F2, F3, F4, algebra]

2.1 [Assembly and scope] Step 1.1 is (a), step 1.2 is (b); only the declared composite, its pure preparations and the cited mathematics were used, and no dynamics, apparatus or empirical input entered, which is the scope statement (c). [step 1.1, step 1.2] ∎

## Remarks

- **One pair of effects suffices.** Clause (b) exhibits a single pair of
  local rank-one effects that detects the correlation; the two-outcome
  measurements with effects $(P,I-P)$ and $(P',I-P')$ have joint law
  $(0,s_{1}^{2},s_{2}^{2},1-s_{1}^{2}-s_{2}^{2})$
  in the ordering $(+,+),(+,-),(-,+),(-,-)$ for the unit vector $\Psi$.
  All entries are nonnegative because $\sum_{r}s_{r}^{2}=1$, and the first
  entry differs from $s_{1}^{2}s_{2}^{2}$.
- **No converse beyond pure states.** The theorem concerns pure preparations;
  for mixed preparations no analogous factorization criterion is asserted.

The statement asserts no dynamics, no interaction, no apparatus realization, no measured correlation and no empirical fact; it is a conditional computation in the declared model.

items.title: Local instruments and no-signalling: operations on one factor do not change the other factor's local statistics
items.statement:
## Statement

Adopt the framework's composition and measurement readings for a declared
composite of two distinguishable subsystems $A,B$ with assigned spaces $H,K$
([[def-nrqm-composites-framework-composite-systems-and-local-readouts]],
[[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]],
[[def-nrqm-composites-framework-reduced-preparations]]), and assume the Axiom
of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), the hypothesis of the cited
mathematics. Let $\rho\in D(H\widehat\otimes K)$ be a preparation of the
declared composite with reduced preparations
$\rho_{A}=\operatorname{Tr}_{K}\rho$, $\rho_{B}=\operatorname{Tr}_{H}\rho$, and
let $(M_{a,r})_{\substack{a\in A_{0}\\ r\in R_{a}}}$ be a declared finite or
countable instrument of subsystem $B$, normalized:
$\sum_{a,r}M_{a,r}^{*}M_{a,r}=I_{K}$ in the strong sense, with effects
$F_{a}:=\sum_{r}M_{a,r}^{*}M_{a,r}$ and outcome probabilities
$p_{a}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{B}F_{a})$. Then:
 
**(a) The local extension.** The family
$(I_{H}\otimes M_{a,r})_{\substack{a\in A_{0}\\ r\in R_{a}}}$ is a declared
finite or countable instrument of the declared composite, with outcome effects
$F_{a}^{\mathrm{loc}}=I_{H}\otimes F_{a}$, outcome probabilities
$p_{a}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_{a}^{\mathrm{loc}})$, and conditional states
$$\rho_{a}:=\frac{1}{p_{a}}\sum_{r}(I_{H}\otimes M_{a,r})\,\rho\,(I_{H}\otimes M_{a,r})^{*}\qquad(p_{a}>0).$$

**(b) No-signalling.** The discarded-outcome state
$\Phi(\rho):=\sum_{a,r}(I_{H}\otimes M_{a,r})\,\rho\,(I_{H}\otimes M_{a,r})^{*}$
is a preparation of the composite, its reduced preparation on $A$ is unchanged,
$$\operatorname{Tr}_{K}\Phi(\rho)=\operatorname{Tr}_{K}\rho=\rho_{A},$$
and consequently every local outcome law of subsystem $A$ is unchanged:
$$\mu^{A^{\mathrm{loc}}}_{\Phi(\rho)}=\mu^{A^{\mathrm{loc}}}_{\rho}\qquad\text{for every assigned sharp observable }(A,u_{A})\text{ of }A .$$
The same holds with the roles of $A$ and $B$ exchanged.

**(c) Conditional reductions.** If $p_{a}>0$, the conditional state $\rho_{a}$
has reduced preparation $(\rho_{a})_{A}=\operatorname{Tr}_{K}\rho_{a}$ on $A$,
and
$$\sum_{a}p_{a}\,(\rho_{a})_{A}=\rho_{A};$$
the conditional reduced preparations $(\rho_{a})_{A}$ may differ from
$\rho_{A}$, and the recorded outcome $a$ is the classical datum needed to
select them.

**(d) Scope.** Clauses (a)-(c) are conditional consequences of P1, P2 and P3
in the stated readings and of the cited mathematics; they concern declared
instruments of the declared composite. They assert no relativistic causality
principle, no claim that a particular apparatus realizes the declared
instrument, no disturbance of the other factor by any concrete device and no
empirical fact.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The declared composite with assigned spaces $H,K$; a preparation $\rho$; reduced preparations $\rho_{A},\rho_{B}$; a declared finite or countable instrument $(M_{a,r})$ of subsystem $B$ with effects $F_{a}$; the Axiom of Countable Choice.

[F1] **Local extension of an instrument.** For a declared finite or countable instrument $(M_{a,r})$ of subsystem $B$ the family $(I_{H}\otimes M_{a,r})$ is a declared instrument of the declared composite, with effects $I_{H}\otimes F_{a}$ and conditional updates as displayed; this is part of clause (e) of [[def-nrqm-composites-framework-composite-systems-and-local-readouts]] ([[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-local-pvm-tensor-extension]] clause (c)).
 
[F2] **Declared instrument reading.** For a declared countable instrument of a system, the outcome probabilities are $p_{a}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_{a})$ with $F_{a}=M_{a}^{*}M_{a}$ (with the sum over $r$ when the family is doubly indexed), the conditional updates are $\rho\mapsto\frac{1}{p_{a}}\sum_{r}M_{a,r}\rho M_{a,r}^{*}$ for $p_{a}>0$, and the discarded-outcome map $\Phi(\rho)=\sum_{a,r}M_{a,r}\rho M_{a,r}^{*}$ is positive, trace preserving and maps states to states ([[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]] clause (d), [[pthm-nrqm-measurement-countable-kraus-instruments]] clauses (a), (e)).

[F3] **Local trace-preserving maps leave the other reduction fixed.** For bounded operators $(N_{b})_{b\ge1}$ on $K$ with $\sum_{b\le N}N_{b}^{*}N_{b}\to I_{K}$ strongly and a trace-class $R$ on $H\widehat\otimes K$, the series $\sum_{b}(I_{H}\otimes N_{b})R(I_{H}\otimes N_{b})^{*}$ converges in trace norm, its sum $\Phi(R)$ is trace class and $\operatorname{Tr}_{K}\Phi(R)=\operatorname{Tr}_{K}R$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-local-trace-preserving-no-signalling]]).

[F4] **Local readout law.** For every assigned sharp observable $(A,u_{A})$ of subsystem $A$, the local readout law is $\mu^{A^{\mathrm{loc}}}_{\rho'}(B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho'_{A}E_{A}(B))$ for every preparation $\rho'$ of the composite with reduced preparation $\rho'_{A}=\operatorname{Tr}_{K}\rho'$ ([[pthm-nrqm-composites-local-readout-laws-and-reduced-preparations]] clause (a), [[lem-nrqm-composites-separable-partial-trace]] clause (a)).

[F5] **Reduced preparations.** $\rho_{A}=\operatorname{Tr}_{K}\rho$ and $\rho_{B}=\operatorname{Tr}_{H}\rho$ are linear, trace-norm continuous images of $\rho$, and the outcome probabilities of a declared instrument of $B$ read $p_{a}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{B}F_{a})$ ([[def-nrqm-composites-framework-reduced-preparations]] clauses (a), (b), [[lem-nrqm-composites-separable-partial-trace]] clauses (a), (b)).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; read the local extension off the fibered
definition of local instruments, apply the trace-preserving local-map lemma to
the discarded-outcome state to fix the reduction of the untouched factor, and
average the conditional reductions with the outcome probabilities.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F5].

1.1 [Extension and discarded map] By [F1] the family $(I_{H}\otimes M_{a,r})$ is a declared instrument of the composite with effects $I_{H}\otimes F_{a}$ and conditional states $\rho_{a}$ for $p_{a}>0$; by [F2] its discarded-outcome map $\Phi$ is positive and trace preserving, so $\Phi(\rho)$ is a preparation of the composite; and re-indexing the doubly indexed family as a sequence $(N_{b})$ on $K$ with $\sum_{b\le N}N_{b}^{*}N_{b}\to I_{K}$ strongly, [F3] gives $\operatorname{Tr}_{K}\Phi(\rho)=\operatorname{Tr}_{K}\rho=\rho_{A}$. This is (a) together with the first assertion of (b); likewise $p_{a}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_{a}^{\mathrm{loc}})=\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{B}F_{a})$ by [F5]. [given, F1, F2, F3, F5, algebra]

2.1 [No-signalling] Let $(A,u_{A})$ be an assigned sharp observable of $A$. By step 1.1 the state $\Phi(\rho)$ has reduced preparation $\rho_{A}$, so [F4] gives $\mu^{A^{\mathrm{loc}}}_{\Phi(\rho)}(B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{A}E_{A}(B))=\mu^{A^{\mathrm{loc}}}_{\rho}(B)$ for every Borel $B$: no local A-statistic changes under the discarded local instrument. This is (b). [given, F4, step 1.1, algebra]

2.2 [Conditional reductions] For $p_{a}>0$ the conditional state $\rho_{a}$ of [F2] satisfies $p_{a}\rho_{a}=\sum_{r}(I_{H}\otimes M_{a,r})\rho(I_{H}\otimes M_{a,r})^{*}$, so by linearity and trace-norm continuity of $\operatorname{Tr}_{K}$ from [F5] one has $p_{a}(\rho_{a})_{A}=\operatorname{Tr}_{K}\sum_{r}(I_{H}\otimes M_{a,r})\rho(I_{H}\otimes M_{a,r})^{*}$; summing over $a$ and using the trace-norm convergence of the discarded series of [F3] gives $\sum_{a}p_{a}(\rho_{a})_{A}=\operatorname{Tr}_{K}\Phi(\rho)=\rho_{A}$ by step 1.1. This is (c); the exchanged-roles form of (b) is the same argument with $H$ and $K$ interchanged. [given, F2, F3, F5, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 [Assembly and scope] Step 1.1 is (a), step 2.1 is (b), step 2.2 is (c), and (d) records that only the declared readings and the cited mathematics were used, with no causality or apparatus claim. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 2.2] ∎
