items.title: Declared marked two-component model: path components, marker states, phase family, detection weights and fringe visibility
items.statement:
## Definition

Adopt the framework's composition and state readings for a declared composite
of two distinguishable subsystems
([[def-nrqm-composites-framework-composite-systems-and-local-readouts]],
[[def-nrqm-composites-framework-reduced-preparations]]), the kinematics and
massive-particle model of P5 for a particle subsystem of spin label
$s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32,\dots\}$ with mass parameter $m>0$ and space
$H_{s}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$, $r=2s+1$
([[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]]), and
the preparation and apparatus discipline P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]). Assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). In the model below the particle
subsystem is $A$ and the marker subsystem is $B$. The following vocabulary is
used by this page.
 
**(a) Position readout of the particle factor.** The model's componentwise
position family has joint spectral projection valued measure $G$ on the Borel
sets of $\mathbb R^{3}$, with
$$G(B)=M_{\mathbf 1_{B}},\qquad \mu^{G}_{\psi}(B)=\|G(B)\psi\|^{2}=\int_{B}\|\psi(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\,dx$$
for $\psi\in H_{s}$ of unit norm and Borel $B\subseteq\mathbb R^{3}$, read in
the metre unit of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]
([[pthm-nrqm-kinematics-spin-s-outcome-laws]] clause (b),
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b)). A
**declared detection bin** is a Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R^{3}$; the
**local position-bin effect** of the declared composite is the bounded effect
$G(B)\otimes I_{K}$ of [[def-nrqm-composites-framework-composite-systems-and-local-readouts]]
clause (d), and the **detection weight** of a preparation $\rho'$ of the
composite is
$$p_{\rho'}(B):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho'\,(G(B)\otimes I_{K})\bigr)\in[0,1],$$
the reading of clause (iv) of P2 for that local effect.
 
**(b) Declared marked two-component model.** A **declared marked
two-component model** of the arrangement consists of: two unit vectors
$\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\in H_{s}$, the **path components** relative to the declared
pair of alternative path conditions; and two unit vectors $e_{1},e_{2}\in K$,
the **marker states** correlated with the alternatives. The assignment of
$\psi_{1},\psi_{2},e_{1},e_{2}$ and of the alternatives is declared apparatus
data in the sense of P7; it is not computed from the framework, and no element
of this definition asserts that a particle described by the model "took" one
of the two alternatives. A declared marked model is **overlap-normalized**
when $\langle\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\rangle=0$, and **trivially marked** when
$|\langle e_{1},e_{2}\rangle|=1$.
 
**(c) Phase family and marked preparations.** For $\varphi\in\mathbb R$ put
$$\Psi(\varphi):=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}\Bigl(\kappa(\psi_{1}\otimes e_{1})+e^{i\varphi}\kappa(\psi_{2}\otimes e_{2})\Bigr)\in H_{s}\widehat\otimes K,$$
where $\kappa$ is the embedding of [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]].
Define the **admissible phase set** $I:=\{\varphi\in\mathbb R:\Psi(\varphi)\ne0\}$. It is nonempty: $\Psi(0)+\Psi(\pi)=\sqrt2\,\kappa(\psi_1\otimes e_1)\ne0$, so those two vectors cannot both vanish, using $e^{i\pi}=-1$ from [[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]]. The **marked preparation at an admissible phase $\varphi\in I$** is the state assigned to the nonzero vector $\Psi(\varphi)$,
$$\rho(\varphi):=\widehat\rho\bigl(\Psi(\varphi)\bigr)=\frac{T_{\Psi(\varphi),\Psi(\varphi)}}{\|\Psi(\varphi)\|^{2}}\in D(H_{s}\widehat\otimes K)$$
([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]] clause (c)); the phase
$\varphi$ is read in radians (dimensionless). The **marker-carried which-path
preparation** is the statistical mixture
$$\rho_{\mathrm{mix}}:=\tfrac12\,T_{\psi_{1}\otimes e_{1},\,\psi_{1}\otimes e_{1}}+\tfrac12\,T_{\psi_{2}\otimes e_{2},\,\psi_{2}\otimes e_{2}},$$
a preparation of the declared composite by clause (iii) of P1.
 
**(d) Detection weights of the family.** For a declared detection bin $B$ and admissible phase $\varphi\in I$ put
$$p(\varphi)(B):=p_{\rho(\varphi)}(B)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho(\varphi)(G(B)\otimes I_{K})\bigr),\qquad p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B):=p_{\rho_{\mathrm{mix}}}(B)=\tfrac12\bigl(\langle G(B)\psi_{1},\psi_{1}\rangle+\langle G(B)\psi_{2},\psi_{2}\rangle\bigr).$$
The numbers $p(\varphi)(B)$ and $p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B)$ lie in $[0,1]$; they are
probabilities of the declared model, not measured frequencies.
 
**(e) Fringe visibility.** The **fringe visibility of the declared phase
family at the bin $B$** is
$$V(B):=\frac{\sup_{\varphi\in I}p(\varphi)(B)-\inf_{\varphi\in I}p(\varphi)(B)}{\sup_{\varphi\in I}p(\varphi)(B)+\inf_{\varphi\in I}p(\varphi)(B)}\qquad\text{whenever }\sup_{\varphi\in I}p(\varphi)(B)+\inf_{\varphi\in I}p(\varphi)(B)>0,$$
and is left undefined otherwise; all extrema, including the denominator, are taken over the nonempty admissible phase set $I$ of clause (c). The number $V(B)$ is a property of the declared model
and the declared bin, read as the modulation contrast of the family of
probabilities; it is not a measured visibility and carries no statement about
an apparatus.
 
**(f) Status.** Clauses (a)-(e) fix the model vocabulary. The path components,
marker states and the identification of a concrete apparatus with the declared
model are declared and tested inputs in the sense of clauses (i)-(iii) of P7;
no dynamics, no interaction, no environment, no detector response, no counts
and no empirical result is asserted. In particular the model does not claim
that the marker is measured or read out, that the alternatives are physically
realized, or that the loss of contrast described by $V$ is caused by any
particular process; the quantitative statement about $V$ is the content of a
separate theorem of this page.

items.title: Marker overlap contracts the cross term: the detection law and the visibility bound of an overlap-normalized marked model
items.statement:
## Statement

Adopt the declared marked two-component model of
[[def-nrqm-composites-marker-model-and-fringe-visibility]] with unit path
components $\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\in H_{s}$, unit marker states $e_{1},e_{2}\in K$,
phase family $\rho(\varphi)$, marker-carried which-path preparation
$\rho_{\mathrm{mix}}$, and a declared detection bin $B$. Assume the model is
**overlap-normalized**, $\langle\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\rangle=0$, and assume the
Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Put
$$\gamma(B):=\langle e_{1},e_{2}\rangle\,\langle G(B)\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\rangle,\qquad p_{j}(B):=\langle G(B)\psi_{j},\psi_{j}\rangle\quad(j=1,2),\qquad p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B)=\tfrac12\bigl(p_{1}(B)+p_{2}(B)\bigr).$$
Then:
 
**(a) Unit-norm phase family.** $\|\Psi(\varphi)\|=1$ for every $\varphi$, so
$\rho(\varphi)=T_{\Psi(\varphi),\Psi(\varphi)}$.
 
**(b) Detection law.** For every $\varphi$,
$$p(\varphi)(B)=p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B)+\operatorname{Re}\bigl(e^{-i\varphi}\gamma(B)\bigr).$$
 
**(c) Contraction of the cross term.** For every $\varphi$,
$$\bigl|p(\varphi)(B)-p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B)\bigr|\le|\gamma(B)|\le|\langle e_{1},e_{2}\rangle|\sqrt{p_{1}(B)p_{2}(B)}\le|\langle e_{1},e_{2}\rangle|\,p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B).$$
In particular, if $e_{1}\perp e_{2}$, then $p(\varphi)(B)=p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B)$
for every $\varphi$: the marked detection law is exactly the which-path law.
 
**(d) Visibility.** Writing $\gamma(B)=|\gamma(B)|e^{i\theta}$ with
$\theta\in[0,2\pi)$, one has
$$\sup_{\varphi}p(\varphi)(B)=p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B)+|\gamma(B)|,\qquad \inf_{\varphi}p(\varphi)(B)=p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B)-|\gamma(B)|,$$
so that, whenever $p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B)>0$, the fringe visibility of clause (e)
of the definition is
$$V(B)=\frac{|\gamma(B)|}{p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B)}=|\langle e_{1},e_{2}\rangle|\,\frac{|\langle G(B)\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\rangle|}{p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B)}\le|\langle e_{1},e_{2}\rangle| .$$
 
**(e) Extremes.** If the model is trivially marked,
$|\langle e_{1},e_{2}\rangle|=1$, then $V(B)=\frac{|\langle G(B)\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\rangle|}{p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B)}\le1$;
if $e_{1}\perp e_{2}$, then $V(B)=0$ for every bin with $p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B)>0$.
 
**(f) Scope.** Clauses (a)-(e) are conditional computations in the declared
model. They assert no measured pattern, no trial counts, no statistical
analysis, no decoherence mechanism, no irreversibility and no which-path
ontology, and they contain no empirical claim.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The declared overlap-normalized marked model with unit $\psi_{1},\psi_{2},e_{1},e_{2}$, $\langle\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\rangle=0$; a declared detection bin $B$; the phase family and preparations of the model definition; the Axiom of Countable Choice.

[F1] **Model data.** $\Psi(\varphi)=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}(\kappa(\psi_{1}\otimes e_{1})+e^{i\varphi}\kappa(\psi_{2}\otimes e_{2}))$, $\rho(\varphi)=\widehat\rho(\Psi(\varphi))$, $\rho_{\mathrm{mix}}=\frac12T_{\psi_{1}\otimes e_{1},\psi_{1}\otimes e_{1}}+\frac12T_{\psi_{2}\otimes e_{2},\psi_{2}\otimes e_{2}}$, $p(\varphi)(B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho(\varphi)(G(B)\otimes I_{K}))$, $p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B)=\frac12(p_{1}(B)+p_{2}(B))$, and $G(B)$ is the position spectral projection with $p_{j}(B)=\|G(B)\psi_{j}\|^{2}\in[0,1]$ ([[def-nrqm-composites-marker-model-and-fringe-visibility]] clauses (a)-(d), [[pthm-nrqm-kinematics-spin-s-outcome-laws]] clause (b)).

[F2] **Marker contraction.** Let $\Psi_{\alpha,\beta}:=\alpha\,\kappa(a\otimes e_{1})+\beta\,\kappa(b\otimes e_{2})$ with unit $a,b\in L^{2}(D)$ and $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb C$; then the reduced weight on the first factor is $\rho=|\alpha|^{2}T_{a,a}+|\beta|^{2}T_{b,b}+\alpha\overline\beta\langle e_{1},e_{2}\rangle T_{a,b}+\overline\alpha\beta\langle e_{2},e_{1}\rangle T_{b,a}$, and $\operatorname{tr}\rho=\|\Psi_{\alpha,\beta}\|^{2}=|\alpha|^{2}+|\beta|^{2}+2\operatorname{Re}(\alpha\overline\beta\langle a,b\rangle\langle e_{1},e_{2}\rangle)$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-marker-overlap-contraction]] clauses (a), (b) and the closing display).

[F3] **Local readout law.** For every assigned sharp observable $(A,u_{A})$ of the particle factor with spectral projection valued measure $E_{A}$, $\operatorname{tr}(\rho'(E_{A}(C)\otimes I_{K}))=\operatorname{tr}(\rho'_{A}E_{A}(C))$ for every preparation $\rho'$ of the composite with reduced preparation $\rho'_{A}$ and every Borel $C$; in particular for the position spectral projection $G(B)$ ([[pthm-nrqm-composites-local-readout-laws-and-reduced-preparations]] clause (a), [[lem-nrqm-composites-separable-partial-trace]] clause (a)).

[F4] **Elementary tensor facts.** For the embedding $\kappa$ one has $\langle\kappa(x\otimes y),\kappa(x'\otimes y')\rangle=\langle x,x'\rangle\langle y,y'\rangle$ on elementary tensors, and $T_{\kappa(x\otimes y),\kappa(x\otimes y)}$ is the rank-one projection of the product vector ([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]] clauses (a), (b), [[lem-nrqm-composites-separable-partial-trace]] clause (c)).

[F5] **Cauchy-Schwarz.** For vectors in a complex inner product space $|\langle x,y\rangle|\le\|x\|\,\|y\|$ ([[thm-cauchy-schwarz-for-real-and-complex-inner-product-spaces]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; apply the marker contraction lemma with
$\alpha=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}$, $\beta=\frac{e^{i\varphi}}{\sqrt2}$ and the
orthogonality of the path components to obtain the unit norm and the reduced
weight, convert the weight into the composite detection law by the local
readout law, bound the cross term by Cauchy-Schwarz, and evaluate the
supremum and infimum of the resulting cosine modulation.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F5].

1.1 [Unit norm and reduced weight] Apply [F2] with $a=\psi_{1}$, $b=\psi_{2}$, $\alpha=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}$ and $\beta=\frac{e^{i\varphi}}{\sqrt2}$. Since $\langle\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\rangle=0$ and $\|e_{1}\|=\|e_{2}\|=1$, the closing display of [F2] gives $\|\Psi(\varphi)\|^{2}=1+2\operatorname{Re}(\alpha\overline\beta\langle\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\rangle\langle e_{1},e_{2}\rangle)=1$, which is (a) and proves that the admissible phase set of the model is $I=\mathbb R$; moreover the reduced weight is $\rho(\varphi)_{A}=\frac12T_{\psi_{1},\psi_{1}}+\frac12T_{\psi_{2},\psi_{2}}+\frac12e^{-i\varphi}\langle e_{1},e_{2}\rangle T_{\psi_{1},\psi_{2}}+\frac12e^{i\varphi}\langle e_{2},e_{1}\rangle T_{\psi_{2},\psi_{1}}$ by clause (a) of [F2]. [given, F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 [Detection law] By [F3], $p(\varphi)(B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho(\varphi)(G(B)\otimes I_{K}))=\operatorname{tr}(\rho(\varphi)_{A}G(B))$; since $G(B)$ is a bounded self-adjoint operator with $G(B)=M_{\mathbf 1_{B}}$ and $T_{x,y}$ pairs as $\operatorname{tr}(T_{x,y}G(B))=\langle G(B)x,y\rangle$ by [F4], the weight of step 1.1 gives $p(\varphi)(B)=\frac12p_{1}(B)+\frac12p_{2}(B)+\operatorname{Re}(e^{-i\varphi}\langle e_{1},e_{2}\rangle\langle G(B)\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\rangle)=p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B)+\operatorname{Re}(e^{-i\varphi}\gamma(B))$, which is (b). [given, F1, F3, F4, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 [Cross-term contraction] For every $\varphi$, $|p(\varphi)(B)-p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B)|=|\operatorname{Re}(e^{-i\varphi}\gamma(B))|\le|\gamma(B)|$; and $|\gamma(B)|=|\langle e_{1},e_{2}\rangle|\,|\langle G(B)\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\rangle|\le|\langle e_{1},e_{2}\rangle|\,\|G(B)\psi_{1}\|\,\|\psi_{2}\|=|\langle e_{1},e_{2}\rangle|\sqrt{p_{1}(B)}$ and also $|\langle G(B)\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\rangle|\le\sqrt{p_{1}(B)p_{2}(B)}$ by two applications of [F5], since $\|G(B)\psi_{2}\|=\sqrt{p_{2}(B)}$; and $\sqrt{p_{1}p_{2}}\le\frac12(p_{1}+p_{2})=p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B)$ by the elementary inequality $2\sqrt{uv}\le u+v$. This proves (c); if $e_{1}\perp e_{2}$ then $\gamma(B)=0$, so $p(\varphi)(B)=p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B)$ for every $\varphi$. [given, F1, F5, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 [Visibility] Write $\gamma(B)=|\gamma(B)|e^{i\theta}$ when $\gamma(B)\ne0$; then $\operatorname{Re}(e^{-i\varphi}\gamma(B))=|\gamma(B)|\cos(\theta-\varphi)$, whose supremum over $\varphi\in\mathbb R$ is $|\gamma(B)|$ (attained at $\varphi=\theta$) and whose infimum is $-|\gamma(B)|$ (attained at $\varphi=\theta+\pi$); when $\gamma(B)=0$ the function is identically zero and the same formulae hold. Hence $\sup_{\varphi}p(\varphi)(B)=p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B)+|\gamma(B)|$ and $\inf_{\varphi}p(\varphi)(B)=p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B)-|\gamma(B)|$, and if $p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B)>0$ the definition of the visibility gives $V(B)=|\gamma(B)|/p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B)$; the bound $V(B)\le|\langle e_{1},e_{2}\rangle|$ is step 3.1. This is (d), and (e) is the special case $|\langle e_{1},e_{2}\rangle|=1$ together with $|\langle G(B)\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\rangle|\le\|G(B)\psi_{1}\|\|\psi_{2}\|\le1$ and the case $e_{1}\perp e_{2}$. [given, F1, step 2.1, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 [Assembly and scope] Step 1.1 is (a), step 2.1 is (b), step 3.1 is (c), step 4.1 is (d), (e); only the declared model, its overlap-normalized hypothesis and the cited mathematics were used, with no measured pattern, count or mechanism asserted, which is (f). [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1] ∎

## Remarks

- **What the bound does and does not say.** The factor $|\langle e_{1},e_{2}\rangle|$
  is an upper bound on the visibility of the declared phase family; the actual
  visibility also contains the overlap factor
  $|\langle G(B)\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\rangle|/p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B)$ of the path
  components at the bin, so a large marker overlap alone does not guarantee a
  visible fringe and a small marker overlap alone does not by itself describe a
  measured pattern.
- **No mechanism claim.** The marker is part of the declared preparation; the
  computation exhibits the correlation between the marker state and the path
  component as the origin of the reduced contrast in the model. It asserts no
  dynamical decoherence process, no irreversibility and no preference among
  interpretations of the alternatives.

items.title: Scope and empirical status of the composites page: adopted readings, derived results, and deferred content
items.statement:
## Remarks

- **Adopted readings.** The page adopts the composition clause of P1
  ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]]) for a declared pair of
  distinguishable subsystems, together with the observable and probability
  postulate P2 and the ideal conditional-measurement postulate P3 in the
  readings of [[def-nrqm-composites-framework-composite-systems-and-local-readouts]];
  the reduced preparations of [[def-nrqm-composites-framework-reduced-preparations]];
  and, for the marked interference model,
  [[def-nrqm-composites-marker-model-and-fringe-visibility]], whose path
  components, marker states and detector bin are declared apparatus data under
  P7 ([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]). The composition
  assignment, the local readout convention and the marked model are adopted,
  not derived from the rest of the framework or from observation.
- **Derived results.** The conditional results of the page are the Schmidt
  reduction, purity criterion and exact pure separability/product equivalence for pure preparations
  ([[pthm-nrqm-composites-schmidt-reduction-and-pure-entanglement]]), the
  identification of local readout laws with the laws of the reduced
  preparation and its converse
  ([[pthm-nrqm-composites-local-readout-laws-and-reduced-preparations]]), the
  invariance of the untouched factor's reduced preparation under discarded
  local instruments, with the conditional reductions averaging back to it
  ([[pthm-nrqm-composites-local-instruments-and-no-signalling]]), and the
  contraction of the marker cross term with the visibility bound
  ([[pthm-nrqm-composites-marker-overlap-and-visibility-bound]]). Each is
  conditional on its stated hypotheses, including the choice hypotheses of the
  cited mathematics.
- **Empirical status.** No item of the page reports an experiment, a count, a
  calibration or a measured correlation, and none is a proof about nature. The
  detection weights and the visibility of the marked model are probabilities
  and contrasts of a declared model; whether a concrete interferometer
  realizes a marked model with particular components, marker states and bin is
  a tested identification with uncertainty in the sense of clauses (i)-(iii)
  of P7, and a comparison of the model with recorded data would require the
  sampling, efficiency, resolution and background qualifications of the
  apparatus, which this page does not supply.
- **Localized detections and accumulated distributions.** The detection
  weights of the page are probabilities for one trial of the declared model.
  An interference pattern is a property of the accumulated distribution of
  many detections, not of a single event, and a finite sample can fail a
  declared fringe criterion with positive probability under ordinary
  independent sampling even when the model is correct; nothing in the page
  draws a statistical conclusion from the displayed probabilities.
- **No-signalling is a model statement.** The invariance proved in
  [[pthm-nrqm-composites-local-instruments-and-no-signalling]] is a statement
  about declared local instruments of the adopted framework and its
  mathematics. It is not a relativistic causality principle, does not assert
  anything about spacelike separation, and does not by itself exclude
  alternative models; the conditional changes of the measured factor's partner
  are the correlations of the model, and every interpretation of the
  alternatives, of the marker and of "which path" is outside the page.
- **Deferred content.** The following are outside this pair and are not
  supplied or assumed here: setting-independent local-response models and the
  classical-versus-quantum Bell comparison, with specified angles and
  finite-data caveats, which belong to the later Bell-models pair; a general
  theory of mixed-state separability, entanglement measures and separability
  criteria beyond the definition given in
  [[def-nrqm-composites-separable-and-entangled-states]]; the exchange
  sectors and exclusion statements for identical particles; quantum circuits,
  teleportation and computation; and any dynamics, interaction or open-system
  model of decoherence, the marked model of this page being a kinematic
  preparation model.

items.title: The spin singlet of two declared spin-half factors: directional correlations, perfect anti-correlation and setting-independent marginals
items.statement:
## Statement

Adopt the framework's composition, state and measurement readings for the
internal factors of two declared spin-half particles
([[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-tensor-spin-composition]],
[[def-nrqm-composites-framework-composite-systems-and-local-readouts]],
[[def-nrqm-composites-framework-reduced-preparations]],
[[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]]),
and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$V=\mathbb C^{2}$ be a declared spin-half internal factor with orthonormal
basis $(e_{+},e_{-})$ and spin matrices $J_{i}=\tfrac12\sigma_{i}$ of
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]], so that
$S_{i}:=\hbar J_{i}$ and, for a unit vector $n\in\mathbb R^{3}$,
$S_{n}:=\sum_{i}n_{i}S_{i}$; let the declared composite of the two internal
factors be $V\widehat\otimes V$ with the local spin observables
$S_{n}\otimes I$ and $I\otimes S_{m}$, read as bounded assigned sharp
observables of the two factors with unit $\mathrm{J\,s}$
([[def-nrqm-angular-momentum-framework-angular-momentum-observables]] clause
(c), [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]). Put
$$\Psi:=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}\bigl(\kappa(e_{+}\otimes e_{-})-\kappa(e_{-}\otimes e_{+})\bigr),\qquad \rho:=T_{\Psi,\Psi}\in D(V\widehat\otimes V),$$
the **singlet preparation**, and let $\rho_{A}=\operatorname{Tr}_{B}\rho$,
$\rho_{B}=\operatorname{Tr}_{A}\rho$ be its reduced preparations. Then:
 
**(a) Singlet data.** $\Psi$ is a unit vector; $S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{i}\Psi=0$ for
all $i$; $\rho_{A}=\rho_{B}=\tfrac12 I$; and the Schmidt expansion of $\Psi$
is $\Psi=\tfrac{1}{\sqrt2}\bigl(\kappa(e_{+}\otimes e_{-})-\kappa(e_{-}\otimes e_{+})\bigr)$
with two equal coefficients, so $\Psi$ is not a product vector and both
reduced preparations are mixed with $\operatorname{tr}\rho_{A}^{2}=\tfrac12$.
 
**(b) Joint directional laws.** For unit vectors $a,b\in\mathbb R^{3}$ with
$\cos\theta=a\cdot b$ and for the two-outcome local measurements
$(P_{a,\pm},P_{a,\mp})$ and $(P_{b,\pm},P_{b,\mp})$ of the observables
$S_{a}\otimes I$ and $I\otimes S_{b}$, the joint probabilities are
$$p(+,+)=p(-,-)=\tfrac12\sin^{2}\tfrac{\theta}{2},\qquad p(+,-)=p(-,+)=\tfrac12\cos^{2}\tfrac{\theta}{2},$$
where the first sign refers to the outcome $+\hbar/2$ or $-\hbar/2$ of
$S_{a}\otimes I$ and the second to that of $I\otimes S_{b}$;
in particular the four numbers are nonnegative and sum to one.
 
**(c) Correlation function.** With the product $\sigma\tau$ of the two sign
labels,
$$\mathbb E(a,b):=\sum_{\sigma,\tau\in\{\pm\}}\sigma\tau\,p(\sigma,\tau) =-\cos\theta=-a\cdot b .$$
In particular $\mathbb E(a,a)=-1$ and $\mathbb E(a,-a)=+1$: the outcomes are
perfectly anti-correlated for equal directions.
 
**(d) Setting-independent marginals.** The marginal laws are
$p_{A}(\pm)=\tfrac12$ and $p_{B}(\pm)=\tfrac12$, independent of $b$ and of
$a$ respectively; the reduced preparations $\rho_{A}=\rho_{B}=\tfrac12 I$ are
unchanged by performing the local measurement on the other factor and
discarding its record, in agreement with
[[pthm-nrqm-composites-local-instruments-and-no-signalling]] clause (b).
 
**(e) Scope.** This is a thought experiment of the declared framework: the
composite is an internal-factor composite, the particles are not assigned
spatial positions or worldlines here, and no spatial separation, temporal
order, relativistic consideration, measurement or recorded data enters. The
computation asserts no empirical correlation and draws no conclusion about
nature; in particular it makes no claim about the completeness of the
framework or about any hidden-variable model.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The declared spin-half internal factor $V=\mathbb C^{2}$ with basis $(e_{+},e_{-})$ and the spin matrices $S_{i}=\hbar J_{i}$; the declared composite $V\widehat\otimes V$ with local observables $S_{n}\otimes I$, $I\otimes S_{m}$; the singlet vector $\Psi$ and preparation $\rho$; unit directions $a,b$; the Axiom of Countable Choice.

[F1] **Finite spin-half matrices.** $J_{i}=\frac12\sigma_{i}$ is self-adjoint on $V$ with $J_{z}e_{\pm}=\pm\frac12e_{\pm}$, $J_{+}e_{-}=e_{+}$, $J_{+}e_{+}=0$, and $\sigma_{i}\sigma_{j}=\delta_{ij}I+i\sum_{k}\varepsilon_{ijk}\sigma_{k}$, so $S_{n}=\frac{\hbar}{2}n\cdot\sigma$ with $(n\cdot\sigma)^{2}=I$ ([[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clauses (a), (b), (e)).

[F2] **Directional outcome laws.** For every unit $n$ the operator $S_{n}$ is bounded self-adjoint with spectrum $\hbar\{-\frac12,\frac12\}$ and spectral projections $P_{n,\pm}=\frac12(I\pm n\cdot\sigma)$; for every unit $\psi\in V$, $\mu^{S_{n}}_{\psi}(\{\pm\hbar/2\})=\|P_{n,\pm}\psi\|^{2}=\frac12(1\pm\langle(n\cdot\sigma)\psi,\psi\rangle)$ ([[pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-spin-spectra-and-outcome-laws]] clauses (a), (c)).

[F3] **Tensor composition.** The composite internal factor $V\widehat\otimes V$ carries the tensor-product representation; the local operators $S_{n}\otimes I$ and $I\otimes S_{m}$ are bounded self-adjoint, and $\langle\kappa(x\otimes y),\kappa(x'\otimes y')\rangle=\langle x,x'\rangle\langle y,y'\rangle$; the singlet vector is the vector displayed in the statement, with $S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{i}\Psi=0$ and the stated expansion ([[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-tensor-spin-composition]] clauses (a), (b), (d), [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]] clauses (a), (b)).

[F4] **Partial trace and reductions.** $\operatorname{Tr}_{B}T_{u\otimes v,u'\otimes v'}=\langle v,v'\rangle T_{u,u'}$, and for unit $\Psi=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}(\kappa(e_{+}\otimes e_{-})-\kappa(e_{-}\otimes e_{+}))$ the reduced preparations are $\rho_{A}=\frac12T_{e_{+},e_{+}}+\frac12T_{e_{-},e_{-}}$ and $\rho_{B}=\frac12T_{e_{-},e_{-}}+\frac12T_{e_{+},e_{+}}$; the purity criterion gives $\operatorname{tr}\rho_{A}^{2}=\frac12$ and shows $\Psi$ is not a product vector ([[lem-nrqm-composites-separable-partial-trace]] clause (c), [[pthm-nrqm-composites-schmidt-reduction-and-pure-entanglement]] clauses (a), (b)).

[F5] **Joint local laws.** For two declared finite-outcome measurements of the factors with effect families $(F_{i})$ and $(F'_{j})$, the joint outcome probabilities in $\rho$ are $\operatorname{tr}(\rho(F_{i}\otimes F'_{j}))$; for rank-one projections $F=T_{x,x}$, $F'=T_{y,y}$ this equals $|\langle\Psi,\kappa(x\otimes y)\rangle|^{2}$ ([[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]] clause (d), [F4] of [[pthm-nrqm-composites-local-statistics-of-products-and-entangled-preparations]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]] clause (e)).

[F6] **No-signalling.** A declared instrument of one factor leaves the reduced preparation of the other factor unchanged when its record is discarded ([[pthm-nrqm-composites-local-instruments-and-no-signalling]] clause (b)).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; read the singlet's reduced preparations off the
partial trace, project the singlet onto the product of directional spin
eigenstates to obtain the joint laws, and evaluate the correlation sum and the
marginals.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F6].

1.1 [Reduced preparations and purity] By [F3] $\Psi$ is a unit eigenvector of $S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{i}$ with eigenvalue $0$; by [F4], $\rho_{A}=\frac12T_{e_{+},e_{+}}+\frac12T_{e_{-},e_{-}}=\frac12I$ and $\rho_{B}=\frac12I$, with $\operatorname{tr}\rho_{A}^{2}=\frac12$, and $\Psi$ is not a product vector; this is (a). [given, F3, F4, algebra]

1.2 Fix unit $a$ and choose an orthonormal eigenbasis $(u_+,u_-)$ of $a\cdot\sigma$, with eigenvalues $+1,-1$. Write its two columns in the fixed basis $(e_+,e_-)$ as the unitary matrix $W$ and set $\delta=\det W$. Expanding the two elementary tensors gives $\kappa(u_+\otimes u_-)-\kappa(u_-\otimes u_+)=\delta[\kappa(e_+\otimes e_-)-\kappa(e_-\otimes e_+)]$. Orthonormality gives $|\delta|^2=\|u_+\|^2\|u_-\|^2-|\langle u_+,u_-\rangle|^2=1$, by direct two-coordinate expansion. Thus with $\eta=\delta^{-1}$, the fixed vector is $\Psi=\eta[\kappa(u_+\otimes u_-)-\kappa(u_-\otimes u_+)]/\sqrt2$, where $|\eta|=1$. For unit $b$ use $P_{b,\pm}=(I\pm b\cdot\sigma)/2$ from [F2]. This phase changes no projection norm or probability. [given, F1, F2, F3, algebra]

2.1 By step 1.2, $(P_{a,+}\otimes P_{b,+})\Psi=\eta\kappa(u_+\otimes P_{b,+}u_-)/\sqrt2$. Since $|\eta|=1$, [F5] and [F2] give $p(+,+)=\|P_{b,+}u_-\|^2/2=[1+\langle(b\cdot\sigma)u_-,u_-\rangle]/4$. The Pauli identities [F1] give $(a\cdot\sigma)(b\cdot\sigma)+(b\cdot\sigma)(a\cdot\sigma)=2(a\cdot b)I$. Pairing this identity against $u_-$ and using self-adjointness and $(a\cdot\sigma)u_-=-u_-$ gives $\langle(b\cdot\sigma)u_-,u_-\rangle=-a\cdot b$; the same calculation for $u_+$ gives $+a\cdot b$. Applying the other three projection pairs therefore gives $p(+,+)=p(-,-)=(1-a\cdot b)/4=\sin^2(\theta/2)/2$ and $p(+,-)=p(-,+)=(1+a\cdot b)/4=\cos^2(\theta/2)/2$, where $\cos\theta=a\cdot b$. These nonnegative numbers sum to one, proving the unchanged clause (b). [given, F1, F2, F3, F5, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 [Correlation and marginals] Summing with the product signs, $\mathbb E(a,b)=p(+,+)+p(-,-)-p(+,-)-p(-,+)=\frac12\sin^{2}\frac{\theta}{2}+\frac12\sin^{2}\frac{\theta}{2}-\frac12\cos^{2}\frac{\theta}{2}-\frac12\cos^{2}\frac{\theta}{2}=\sin^{2}\frac{\theta}{2}-\cos^{2}\frac{\theta}{2}=-\cos\theta$, which is (c) since $\theta$ is the angle between $a$ and $b$; the marginals are $p_{A}(+)=p(+,+)+p(+,-)=\frac12$ and $p_{A}(-)=\frac12$, and likewise $p_{B}(\pm)=\frac12$, independent of the other direction. The preparations $\rho_{A}=\rho_{B}=\frac12I$ are unchanged by a discarded local instrument on the other factor by [F6]; this is (d). [given, F2, F6, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 [Assembly and scope] Step 1.1 is (a), step 2.1 is (b), step 3.1 is (c), (d); only the declared internal-factor composite and the cited mathematics were used, with no spatial, temporal, relativistic or empirical input, which is (e). [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1] ∎

## Remarks

- **Anti-correlation and the singlet.** For $b=\pm a$ the correlation is $\mp1$,
  the perfect anti-correlation (or correlation for the reversed direction) of
  the model. For $a\perp b$ the correlation vanishes, $\mathbb E=0$.
- **Correlated but not signalling.** The joint laws depend on both directions,
  while each marginal is the fixed law $\frac12$ of the maximally mixed reduced
  preparation: the model's correlations are not a dependence of one factor's
  local statistics on the other factor's setting.
- **Not an experiment.** No counts, apparatus or uncertainty analysis appears;
  a comparison of such a model with recorded data would require a separate
  experiment item with its own preparation, efficiency and sampling
  qualifications, and the Bell comparison belongs to a later page.

items.title: A two-cell marked model: the fringe visibility equals the marker overlap exactly
items.statement:
## Example

Adopt the declared marked two-component model of
[[def-nrqm-composites-marker-model-and-fringe-visibility]] with $s=0$
(scalar particle), $m>0$, $H_{0}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3})$, and the marker space
$K=\mathbb C^{2}$, and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice
([[def-countable-choice]]). Declare the following **two-cell model**:
 
(a) fix a unit vector $\eta\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{2})$ and define the unit path
components
$$\psi_{1}(x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}):=\mathbf 1_{[0,1]}(x_{1})\,\eta(x_{2},x_{3}),\qquad \psi_{2}(x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}):=\bigl(\mathbf 1_{[0,\frac12]}(x_{1})-\mathbf 1_{[\frac12,1]}(x_{1})\bigr)\eta(x_{2},x_{3});$$
 
(b) declare the marker states
$e_{1}:=(1,0)$, $e_{2}:=(\cos\vartheta,\sin\vartheta)$ for a fixed
$\vartheta\in[0,\pi/2]$, so that $\langle e_{1},e_{2}\rangle=\cos\vartheta$;
 
(c) declare the detection bin $B:=[0,\tfrac12]\times\mathbb R^{2}$ with
position effect $G(B)=M_{\mathbf 1_{B}}$.
 
Then:
 
(i) $\psi_{1},\psi_{2}$ are unit vectors with $\langle\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\rangle=0$
and $\|\Psi(\varphi)\|=1$ for every phase $\varphi$, so the model is
overlap-normalized;
 
(ii) $p_{1}(B)=p_{2}(B)=\tfrac12$,
$\langle G(B)\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\rangle=\tfrac12$ and
$p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B)=\tfrac12$, hence
$$p(\varphi)(B)=\tfrac12\bigl(1+\cos\vartheta\cos\varphi\bigr),\qquad V(B)=\cos\vartheta=|\langle e_{1},e_{2}\rangle| :$$
the visibility equals the marker overlap exactly, saturating the bound of
[[pthm-nrqm-composites-marker-overlap-and-visibility-bound]] clause (d);
 
(iii) at $\vartheta=0$ (identical markers) $p(\varphi)(B)=\tfrac12(1+\cos\varphi)$
and $V(B)=1$; at $\vartheta=\pi/2$ (orthogonal markers)
$p(\varphi)(B)=\tfrac12$ for every phase and $V(B)=0$, so the marked detection
law is exactly the which-path law.
 
The profiles, the bin and the marker states are declared idealizations of the
model; the computation asserts no measured pattern, no counts, no detector
response and no empirical result.

## Verification

**Given:** The two-cell model data: unit $\eta$, unit $\psi_{1},\psi_{2}$ as displayed, marker states $e_{1},e_{2}$ with $\langle e_{1},e_{2}\rangle=\cos\vartheta$, bin $B=[0,\frac12]\times\mathbb R^{2}$, phase family $\rho(\varphi)$; the Axiom of Countable Choice.

[L1] **Model readings.** $\Psi(\varphi)=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}(\kappa(\psi_{1}\otimes e_{1})+e^{i\varphi}\kappa(\psi_{2}\otimes e_{2}))$ with $\kappa$ the tensor embedding, and the detection weight is $p(\varphi)(B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho(\varphi)(G(B)\otimes I_{K}))$ with $G(B)=M_{\mathbf 1_{B}}$; the reduced weight of the phase family and its normalization are the ones of [[lem-nrqm-composites-marker-overlap-contraction]] ([[def-nrqm-composites-marker-model-and-fringe-visibility]] clauses (a)-(d), [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]).

[L2] **Visibility data.** For an overlap-normalized model, $\sup_{\varphi}p(\varphi)(B)=p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B)+|\gamma(B)|$, $\inf_{\varphi}p(\varphi)(B)=p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B)-|\gamma(B)|$ and $V(B)=|\gamma(B)|/p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B)$ with $\gamma(B)=\langle e_{1},e_{2}\rangle\langle G(B)\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\rangle$ ([[pthm-nrqm-composites-marker-overlap-and-visibility-bound]] clauses (a), (c), (d)).

[L3] **Flat-profile integrals.** For the displayed profiles and bin, $\|\psi_{j}\|=1$, $\langle\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\rangle=0$, $\langle G(B)\psi_{j},\psi_{j}\rangle=\frac12$ and $\langle G(B)\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\rangle=\frac12$; these are Fubini factorizations of integrals of products of the one-dimensional profiles with the unit function $\eta$ ([[thm-fubini-theorem-for-l-one-on-sigma-finite-product-spaces]], [[pthm-nrqm-kinematics-spin-s-outcome-laws]] clause (b)).

**Proof technique:** direct; evaluate the four flat-profile integrals by Fubini, substitute the marker overlap and the phase family into the contraction theorem's detection law, and read off the visibility and its extremes.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [L1]-[L3].

1.1 [Profile integrals] By [L3], $\|\psi_{1}\|^{2}=\|\mathbf 1_{[0,1]}\|^{2}\|\eta\|^{2}=1$ and $\|\psi_{2}\|^{2}=\|\mathbf 1_{[0,\frac12]}-\mathbf 1_{[\frac12,1]}\|^{2}\|\eta\|^{2}=\frac12+\frac12=1$; $\langle\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\rangle=(\int_{0}^{1}\bigl(\mathbf 1_{[0,\frac12]}-\mathbf 1_{[\frac12,1]}\bigr)dx)\|\eta\|^{2}=\frac12-\frac12=0$; $p_{1}(B)=\int_{0}^{\frac12}dx=\frac12$ and $p_{2}(B)=\int_{0}^{\frac12}dx=\frac12$; and $\langle G(B)\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\rangle=\int_{0}^{\frac12}dx=\frac12$. This is (i) for orthogonality and unit norm, and gives the data of (ii). [given, L3, algebra]

2.1 [Detection law and visibility] By step 1.1 the model is overlap-normalized; the marker theorem clause (a) in [L2] then gives $\|\Psi(\varphi)\|=1$ for every real phase and hence $I=\mathbb R$, so [L1] and [L2] apply with $p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B)=\frac12$ and $\gamma(B)=\cos\vartheta\cdot\frac12$; hence $p(\varphi)(B)=\frac12+\operatorname{Re}(e^{-i\varphi}\frac{\cos\vartheta}{2})=\frac12(1+\cos\vartheta\cos\varphi)$ and $V(B)=|\gamma(B)|/p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B)=\frac{\cos\vartheta/2}{1/2}=\cos\vartheta$, which is (ii); at $\vartheta=0$ and $\vartheta=\pi/2$ the displayed laws and values are the ones of (iii). [given, L1, L2, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 [Assembly] Step 1.1 is (i), step 2.1 is (ii) and (iii); only the declared model and the cited mathematics were used, so no measured pattern, count or apparatus response is asserted. [step 1.1, step 2.1] ∎

items.title: Improper and proper mixtures with the same reduced preparation: the singlet marginal versus a fair random mixture
items.statement:
## Example

Adopt the declared internal-factor composite of two spin-half factors and the
singlet preparation $\rho=T_{\Psi,\Psi}$ of
[[texp-nrqm-composites-singlet-correlations]], with $V=\mathbb C^{2}$,
orthonormal basis $(e_{+},e_{-})$, spin matrices $S_{i}=\hbar J_{i}$ and
$S_{n}=\sum_{i}n_{i}S_{i}$ for unit $n\in\mathbb R^{3}$
([[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]],
[[pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-spin-spectra-and-outcome-laws]]), and let
[[def-nrqm-composites-framework-reduced-preparations]] and
[[pthm-nrqm-composites-schmidt-reduction-and-pure-entanglement]] supply the
reading of the reduced preparations. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice
([[def-countable-choice]]). Declare:
 
(a) the **improper mixture** of factor $A$: the reduced preparation
$\rho_{A}=\operatorname{Tr}_{B}\rho$ of the singlet;
 
(b) the **proper mixture** of factor $A$: the declared preparation in which a
fair classical randomization selects the pure preparation $T_{e_{+},e_{+}}$
with probability $\tfrac12$ and $T_{e_{-},e_{-}}$ with probability $\tfrac12$,
so that
$$\rho_{\mathrm{proper}}:=\tfrac12T_{e_{+},e_{+}}+\tfrac12T_{e_{-},e_{-}};$$
 
(c) the **EPR-type product mixture** of the composite: the declared
preparation
$$M:=\tfrac12T_{e_{+}\otimes e_{-},\,e_{+}\otimes e_{-}}+\tfrac12T_{e_{-}\otimes e_{+},\,e_{-}\otimes e_{+}},$$
in which each factor carries a definite spin along the $z$-axis and the two
spins are opposite.
 
Then:
 
(i) $\rho_{A}=\rho_{\mathrm{proper}}=\tfrac12 I$ and the marginals of $M$ are
$\operatorname{Tr}_{B}M=\tfrac12I=\operatorname{Tr}_{A}M$: the two
preparations of factor $A$ and the marginal of $M$ are the same density
operator, and $\rho$ and $M$ are not the same composite preparation;
 
(ii) for unit directions $a,b$, writing $a_{3}=a\cdot e_{z}$ and
$b_{3}=b\cdot e_{z}$ with $e_{z}$ the direction of the $z$-axis of the basis
$(e_{+},e_{-})$, the directional correlation of the singlet is
$\mathbb E_{\rho}(a,b)=-\cos\theta=-a\cdot b$ while that of the product mixture
is
$$\mathbb E_{M}(a,b)=-\tfrac12a_{3}b_{3}-\tfrac12a_{3}b_{3}=-a_{3}b_{3};$$
in particular $\mathbb E_{\rho}(z,z)=\mathbb E_{M}(z,z)=-1$ but
$\mathbb E_{\rho}(x,x)=-1$ and $\mathbb E_{M}(x,x)=0$ for the orthogonal
direction $x$;
 
(iii) $M$ is a convex combination of the two pure product states
$T_{e_{+}\otimes e_{-},\,\cdot}$ and $T_{e_{-}\otimes e_{+},\,\cdot}$, hence a
separable preparation in the sense of clause (b) of
[[def-nrqm-composites-separable-and-entangled-states]], while $\rho$ is a
non-product pure preparation; and every local readout law of factor $A$ is
the same in $\rho$, in $\rho_{\mathrm{proper}}$ extended by any preparation of
$B$, and in $M$, because all three have the reduced preparation $\tfrac12I$ on
$A$;
 
(iv) consequently the density operator $\tfrac12I$ alone does not determine
whether the preparation of factor $A$ arises as the reduction of an entangled
composite preparation (the improper case) or from a classical randomization
of factor preparations (the proper case): the two cases are distinguished by
the joint statistics with the other factor, not by any local statistic of
$A$.
 
The comparison is a conditional computation of the declared framework; it
asserts no measured correlation, no experiment and no empirical fact.

## Verification

**Given:** The internal-factor composite $V\widehat\otimes V$; the singlet preparation $\rho$ and its reductions; the proper mixture $\rho_{\mathrm{proper}}$; the product mixture $M$; unit directions $a,b$; the Axiom of Countable Choice.

[L1] **Singlet data.** $\rho_{A}=\rho_{B}=\frac12I$ and $\mathbb E_{\rho}(a,b)=-a\cdot b$ for all unit $a,b$ ([[texp-nrqm-composites-singlet-correlations]] clauses (a), (c)).

[L2] **Product reductions and local laws.** For unit $x,y$ one has $\operatorname{Tr}_{B}T_{x\otimes y,x\otimes y}=T_{x,x}$ and $\operatorname{Tr}_{A}T_{x\otimes y,x\otimes y}=T_{y,y}$; the local directional laws read $\mu^{S_{n}}_{\psi}(\{\pm\hbar/2\})=\frac12(1\pm\langle(n\cdot\sigma)\psi,\psi\rangle)$ on $V$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-separable-partial-trace]] clause (c), [[pthm-nrqm-angular-momentum-spin-spectra-and-outcome-laws]] clause (c), [[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clause (e)).

[L3] **Local readout law.** If two preparations of the composite have the same reduced preparation on $A$, then every local readout law of $A$ agrees in the two preparations ([[pthm-nrqm-composites-local-readout-laws-and-reduced-preparations]] clause (a)).

[L4] **Mixtures and separability.** A convex combination $\sum_{j}w_{j}T_{\Psi_{j},\Psi_{j}}$ of pure product preparations with weights $w_{j}\ge0$, $\sum_{j}w_{j}=1$ is a preparation of the composite and a separable state in the sense of clause (b) of [[def-nrqm-composites-separable-and-entangled-states]]; outcome laws are affine in the preparation ([[def-nrqm-composites-separable-and-entangled-states]] clause (c), [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (b)).

[L5] The density expansion into an at most countable positive orthonormal rank-one sum and trace-norm completeness are [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a) and [[thm-trace-class-is-a-two-sided-banach-operator-ideal]] clause 3. Partial trace is trace-norm continuous by [[lem-nrqm-composites-separable-partial-trace]] clause (a).

**Proof technique:** direct; compute the two marginals and the two correlation functions from the product structure, and compare the local readout laws through the common reduced preparation.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [L1]-[L4].

1.1 [Marginals] By [L2], $\operatorname{Tr}_{B}T_{e_{+}\otimes e_{-},e_{+}\otimes e_{-}}=T_{e_{+},e_{+}}$ and $\operatorname{Tr}_{B}T_{e_{-}\otimes e_{+},e_{-}\otimes e_{+}}=T_{e_{-},e_{-}}$, so the linearity of the partial trace gives $\operatorname{Tr}_{B}M=\frac12T_{e_{+},e_{+}}+\frac12T_{e_{-},e_{-}}=\frac12I$; likewise $\operatorname{Tr}_{A}M=\frac12I$. Together with $\rho_{A}=\frac12I$ from [L1] and $\rho_{\mathrm{proper}}=\frac12I$ by definition this is (i). [given, L1, L2, algebra]

1.2 [Correlations of the product mixture] By [L2] and [L4] the joint outcome law of the local measurements of $S_{a}\otimes I$ and $I\otimes S_{b}$ in $M$ is the weighted average of the two product laws, so $\mathbb E_{M}(a,b)=\frac12\langle(a\cdot\sigma)e_{+},e_{+}\rangle\langle(b\cdot\sigma)e_{-},e_{-}\rangle+\frac12\langle(a\cdot\sigma)e_{-},e_{-}\rangle\langle(b\cdot\sigma)e_{+},e_{+}\rangle=\frac12(a_{3})(-b_{3})+\frac12(-a_{3})(b_{3})=-a_{3}b_{3}$; with [L1] this is (ii). [given, L1, L2, L4, algebra]

2.1 [Local indistinguishability and separability] Let $\tau_B$ be any preparation of $B$. Its density expansion is $\tau_B=\sum_jq_jT_{z_j,z_j}$ in trace norm, with unit $z_j$, $q_j>0$ and $\sum_jq_j=1$, by [L5]. The independent extension of the proper mixture is the trace-norm sum $\Omega=\sum_j(q_j/2)(T_{e_+\otimes z_j,e_+\otimes z_j}+T_{e_-\otimes z_j,e_-\otimes z_j})$: every summand is positive, and its trace norm equals its nonnegative trace, so the series converges with trace one by [L4], [L5]. The rank-one reduction formula [L2] and trace-norm continuity [L5] give $\operatorname{Tr}_B\Omega=(T_{e_+,e_+}+T_{e_-,e_-})/2=I_A/2$ and $\operatorname{Tr}_A\Omega=\tau_B$, which need not equal $I_B/2$. Since $\rho$ and $M$ also have reduction $I_A/2$ by [L1] and step 1.1, [L3] proves all local-$A$ readout laws agree for $\rho$, $M$ and this arbitrary-$B$ extension. The displayed convex decomposition makes $M$ separable by [L4], while $\rho$ is non-product and pure by [L1] and the purity criterion. Their joint laws differ at $(x,x)$ by step 1.2. This proves (iii) and (iv) with the full arbitrary-extension claim. [given, L1, L2, L3, L4, L5, step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 [Assembly] Step 1.1 is (i), step 1.2 is (ii), step 2.1 is (iii) and (iv); only the declared framework readings and the cited computations were used, so no measured correlation or empirical fact is asserted. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1] ∎

## Remarks

- **The reduction is not an ensemble decomposition.** Nothing in the example
  presents $\rho_{A}=\frac12I$ as produced by a classical randomization; the
  reduction is the partial trace of the composite preparation, and the
  randomization of the proper mixture is a separate declared preparation of
  factor $A$ that happens to assign the same density operator.
- **Same local state, different composite.** The comparison is a precise
  instance of the general fact that the reduced preparation determines all
  local statistics of its own factor while the joint statistics depend on the
  composite preparation.

## Remarks

- **What the page contains.** Three conditional computations in the declared
  framework: the singlet thought experiment of
  [[texp-nrqm-composites-singlet-correlations]] with its reduced preparations,
  directional joint laws, correlation function and setting-independent
  marginals; the two-cell marked model of
  [[ex-nrqm-composites-marker-overlap-visibility]], where the fringe
  visibility equals the marker overlap exactly and the theorem
  [[pthm-nrqm-composites-marker-overlap-and-visibility-bound]] is saturated;
  and the comparison of
  [[ex-nrqm-composites-improper-versus-proper-mixtures]] between the singlet's
  reduced preparation and a fair random mixture of factor preparations that
  assigns the same density operator.
- **What the page does not contain.** No experiment, no reported count, no
  calibration, no efficiency, no sampling model, no statistical test and no
  measured correlation appears on the page; no item is a report of an observed
  outcome, and none of the computations establishes that the framework or any
  of its postulates describes nature. The model data of the marked example and
  of the singlet are declared idealizations; identifying a concrete apparatus
  with them is a tested identification with uncertainty under P7
  ([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]).
- **Statistics of the displayed probabilities.** The detection weights,
  joint laws and correlation functions are probabilities of the declared
  models for a single trial or for an idealized family of phases. A finite
  sample of trials would require its own sampling model and would show
  fluctuations; no inference, error rate or conclusion is drawn here from the
  displayed numbers, and a measured fringe pattern would concern the
  accumulated distribution of many detections, not a single event.
- **Deferred comparisons.** The Bell-type comparison of the singlet
  correlations with specified local-response models, with its angles,
  finite-data selection and loss caveats, belongs to the later Bell-models
  pair and is neither stated nor assumed here; nor does the page settle any
  interpretation of the alternatives, of the marker or of "which path", and it
  does not model any dynamical decoherence process.
